strategies.name: D1: Pick-Schur causality LMIs, a multi-frequency Nevanlinna-Pick constraint on the lifted (E, P) Gram that ties several frequencies to ONE causal dispersive material, with the f-sum budget as the Nevanlinna mass
strategies.cards: P3 (primary: Lorentzian-mixture windows, M_L as K = 1); P1 (non-dispersive specialisation, added as an extra valid constraint)
strategies.claim: Lemma, verified numerically. Take a passive, causal, local medium whose local response satisfies two conditions. (a) h_x(z) = z chi(x,z) is Herglotz (Im h >= 0 for Im z > 0). (b) The representation is h_x(z) = int dnu_x(t)/(t - z), with nu_x >= 0 and total mass nu_x(R) = s(x). Every Lorentz sum chi = sum_j w_pj^2/(w_0j^2 - z^2 - i g_j z) qualifies, with s = sum_j w_pj^2: the card's oscillator-strength density. Then for ANY frequencies z_1..z_K in Im z > 0, any fields E_j(x) and P_j = chi(x,z_j) E_j, the following (K+1)x(K+1) matrix is PSD at every point: Q_x = [[ s(x), conj(z_j P_j) ], [ z_i P_i, (z_i P_i conj(E_j) - conj(z_j) E_i conj(P_j)) / (z_i - conj(z_j)) ]]. Proof: the Pick matrix of h, augmented by the mass, is the Gram matrix of (1, 1/(t - z_i)) in L^2(nu), so it is PSD. Q_x is its Schur (Hadamard) product with [1; E][1; E]^dagger, which is PSD by the Schur product theorem. Every entry of Q_x is LINEAR in the lifted Gram of (1, E_1..E_K, P_1..P_K) and in s(x). Sums over pixels of a cluster stay PSD. Bound: L3^mix(W) = min over a lifted X >= 0 of sum_j w_j Im F(z_j), with F(z) = -(4i/z) sum_n b_n(z). Constraints: (i) Maxwell at each z_j with the PEC-object Green's function G_obj(z_j); (ii) the cluster LMIs Q_m >= 0; (iii) sum_m s_m <= W w_c^2 A_ann with s_m >= 0; (iv) optionally, run-1 S3's per-frequency gamma_min disk |P_j|^2 <= s Im(conj(E_j) P_j) / y_min(z_j), as its convex lifted form. By the Hashemi/Strekha residue identity, sum_j w_j Im F(z_j) = int sigma_ext(k) W_mix(k) dk, with W_mix = sum_j w_j [L_j(k) + L_j(-k)], a positive Lorentzian-mixture window (the card's L(k) + L(-k) convention, per centre). So R3^mix >= L3^mix / M_mix,bare. K = 1 is the card's M_L. K = 3 to 5 centres across the band with eta_j = k_c B/(2K) approximate the flat window from inside. For P1 (real chi in [0, chi_max], frequency-independent), h = chi z + 0 has a linear term chi z. The Pick-Schur LMI without the mass row still holds (checked), and the stronger equality X_PE,ij = conj(X_PE,ji) (shared real chi) can be added.
strategies.approach: 1. Prove the lemma: Nevanlinna representation for z chi; Gram-matrix form of the augmented Pick matrix; Schur product with the rank-one field Gram; linearity in the lifted variables. Note that it is a necessary condition only, since the Schur product loses information. 2. Show the K = 1 reductions. (a) Without the mass row it becomes Im(z conj(E) P) >= 0, which is exactly the Kuang-Miller conjugate-frequency passivity weighting. (b) With the mass row it becomes the single-point Herglotz disk |z chi|^2 <= s Im(z chi)/Im z. (c) s = 0 forces P = 0, giving the bare object. 3. Build the multi-frequency lifted problem with the PEC-object Green's function. In the angular-harmonic basis G_obj(z) is diagonal in n, with radial kernel (i/4)[J_n(z r<) - (J_n(za)/H_n(za)) H_n(z r<)] H_n(z r>) times the angular factor; normalisation to be verified against cloak2d.coeffs at complex k. 4. Do the radial-design version first: channels decouple per frequency, and each channel's lifted block carries per-ring Pick-Schur LMIs with ring masses s_r shared by all channels. Then the free-form version via the Lagrange dual, with a matrix multiplier Lambda_m >= 0 per (ring x sector) cluster; any multiplier set with a PSD Lagrangian Hessian certifies a bound. 5. Add S3's gamma_min disk per frequency, so that D1 contains the single-frequency S3 relaxation. The new element is the cross-frequency Pick coupling. It forbids the relaxation from choosing unrelated susceptibilities at neighbouring frequencies, e.g. eps ~ 0.5 at one centre and eps ~ 4 at the next without a pole and its mass in between. 6. Sweep W, eta and K, and report L3^mix(W).
strategies.numerical_procedure: Done (scratchpad gen_duality/pick_schur_check.py, summary.json). 20000 random Lorentz media (1 to 3 oscillators, w0 in [0.05, 20], gamma in [1e-3, 1]), K = 1..5 complex frequencies in k_c[0.7, 1.3] + i k_c[1e-3, 0.3]. Minimum normalised eigenvalue: 1.3e-14 for the Pick-Schur LMI and 1.0e-14 for the mass-augmented LMI, so both are valid. A constant real chi gives PSD Pick-Schur eigenvalues (-7.5e-15, 1e-16, 8.46). Caveat found: with 3 points the augmented LMI still accepts s = 0.6 for a true mass of 0.7, so a few points enforce the budget loosely. Health note: invisibility/.venv currently has no site-packages (numpy is missing); the checks ran with .mamba/envs/meep/bin/python, so the venv must be rebuilt before cvxpy runs. Next: (a) a radial-class SDP in cvxpy with hermitian=True, Clarabel and SCS as fallback. N_r = 24 rings, |n| <= 12 using the +/-n symmetry (13 blocks), K = 3. Each channel's lifted block is 1 + 2*K*N_r = 145 complex; per-ring 4x4 LMIs; shared s_r; well under 1 GB. (b) Free-form: dual ascent (L-BFGS on the concave dual, Cholesky PSD check as the certificate) on a polar spectral basis with N ~ 600 per frequency and 8 x 8 ring-sector clusters. (c) Sweep W in {0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 2, 8}, gamma_min in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1}, B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3} and K in {1, 2, 3, 5}, and report the bound at K = 1 against K > 1 to isolate the cross-frequency gain. (d) Adversary: run_lorentz.py designs rescored on M_mix with cloak2d.coeffs at complex k, plus warm-started L = 8 layered optimisation directly on M_mix.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) The lemma holds on 20000 random Lorentz media (done). (ii) K = 1 without the mass row equals Kuang-Miller passivity Im(z conj(E) P) >= 0; with the mass row it equals the single-point Herglotz disk. (iii) W = 0 forces P = 0 and L3 = 1; L3 is non-increasing in W. (iv) Reproduce first: the bare PEC M_L = 5.52 a both from Im F(k~) and from quadrature of sigma_ext [L(k) + L(-k)]; the f-sum integral (2.042035 vs (pi/2) w_p^2, as in S3); and cloak2d b_n at complex k from the G_obj discretisation, to 1e-6. (v) Every baseline Lorentz design (lorentz_W{0.5,2,8}_L4_g0.01.json) must satisfy every cluster LMI when its own fields are substituted (unit test of validity), and must score at or above the bound on the same window. (vi) The K = 1 bound with the gamma_min disk must equal the S3 single-frequency program on identical discretisation.
strategies.expected_tightness: In the budget-binding regime (W = 0.5, where the optimum uses an eps ~ 0.5 layer that needs nearby dispersion) the cross-frequency coupling should raise the K = 1 bound noticeably: a factor of about 1.2-2 is plausible, giving gap ratios of about 1.1-2 on M_mix. At W >= 2 the eps ~ 4 coating needs no dispersion in band, so the gain shrinks toward the single-frequency Strekha-type value. As eta -> 0 at fixed K, single-point relaxations weaken in proportion to Im z, and the Pick coupling between centres is the only band information left. The flat-window conversion still needs out-of-band caps (not claimed here).
strategies.closest_prior: Kuang & Miller PRL 125, 263607 (2020): conjugate-frequency passivity, the K = 1 case. Strekha et al. PRA 110, 063513 (2024): single complex frequency, chi fixed, no dispersion model. Run-1 S3: single-frequency f-sum disk with gamma_min. Zhang, Monticone & Miller 2023 (tutorial Eq. 175c): f-sum constraints in an unstructured volume-T-matrix model. Shim, Kuang, Lin & Miller arXiv 2112.10816: cross-frequency constraints for a FIXED material. Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation has been used for passive material approximation (Gustafsson & Sjoberg NJP 12, 043046, 2010; Ivanenko et al. SIAM J. Appl. Math. 79, 436, 2019), but not inside field-level QCQP bounds. No prior f-sum cloaking bound.
strategies.risk: Medium. (1) The Schur product is lossy, and the lifted (Shor) relaxation can satisfy the LMIs with mixtures; the gain over K = 1 may be small. Measure it before investing in the free-form version. (2) A few points enforce the mass budget loosely (demonstrated). (3) gamma_min enters only through the S3 per-frequency disk, not through the Pick coupling. (4) Windows are Lorentzian mixtures, not flat. (5) SDP size for free-form designs forces the dual route. (6) The bound is for the discretised operator; a convergence study in N_r and n_max is required.

strategies.name: D2: Frequency-independence as cross-constraints: a multi-complex-frequency Strekha dual for the PEC object, with one shared real chi(x) tied across several complex frequencies (the non-dispersive class seen at more than one point)
strategies.cards: P1 (primary: free-form, M_L and Lorentzian-mixture windows); P4 at B > 0 (radial class, channel-block-diagonal version)
strategies.claim: Class (P1 and P4): real, frequency-independent chi(x) in [0, chi_max]. This is the weak-* closure of binary {0, chi_max} patterns, because eps enters only the zeroth-order TM term (card P1). At every complex z the polarisation is P(z) = chi E(z) with the SAME real chi. Hence, for every subregion Omega_m and every frequency pair (i, j), where E_j = E_d(z_j) + G_obj(z_j) P_j is the total field with the PEC object folded into G_obj: (self, binary) int_{Omega_m} [ |P_j|^2/chi_max - conj(E_j) P_j ] = 0 (complex: resistive and reactive parts); (cross, shared real chi) int_{Omega_m} [ P_i conj(E_j) - E_i conj(P_j) ] = 0; (cross, binary) int_{Omega_m} [ P_i conj(P_j)/chi_max - P_i conj(E_j) ] = 0. Bound: for frequencies z_j = k_j + i eta_j in the upper half-plane and weights w_j > 0, M_w = int sigma_ext(k) sum_j w_j [L_j(k) + L_j(-k)] dk = sum_j w_j Im F(z_j) >= max over lambda of g(lambda). Here g is the concave Lagrange dual of min over {P_j} of sum_j w_j Im F_j(P_j) (affine in P_j) subject to all the self and cross constraints. Any lambda with a PSD Lagrangian Hessian is a certificate. R1(M_w) >= g / M_w,bare (M_L,bare = 5.52 a). The new element is the cross-frequency ties, which encode that constant real eps >= 1 is the same material at every complex frequency. Strekha fixes chi at one complex frequency and cannot use this. Optionally, an anchor frequency z_0 = k_c + i Delta with zero objective weight injects effective loss into the near-real (small-eta) scenarios through the ties.
strategies.approach: 1. Build the PEC-object TM Green's function at complex z in the polar spectral basis. It is diagonal in angular index n with an analytic radial kernel; check it against cloak2d.coeffs at complex k for layered designs. 2. Write the incident-plus-object field E_d(z) and the extinction functional Im F(z) as an affine function of P(z), via the forward amplitude of the PEC-object radiation map. 3. Assemble the self constraints of Strekha's Eq. 4 type and the new cross-frequency ties on ring x sector clusters. For radial (P4-type) designs use rings only: everything is block-diagonal in n, and the shared radial chi(r) is expressed by ring-wise ties across BOTH frequencies and channels. 4. Use the Kuang-Miller iteration: start with global constraints, then add the most violated cluster or cross constraint each round. Solve the dual by L-BFGS on g with a Cholesky PSD check, so every iterate with a PSD Hessian is a valid bound. 5. Sweep K (1 = Strekha, 2-4), eta/k_c in {1e-3, 1e-2, 0.05} and the anchor Delta. Measure how much the ties keep the bound from collapsing in proportion to eta, which is Strekha's dw-linear regime. 6. Map the bound against eps_max and b/a (nested-class monotonicity) and against the layered/ceviche adversary scored on the same mixture window.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Polar spectral discretisation on a < r < b: |n| <= 12 to 16, N_r = 24 to 32 Chebyshev or collocation rings, giving N ~ 600-1000 complex unknowns per frequency. K <= 4 keeps the dense Hermitian Hessian at 4000 or less (about 250 MB complex), so a Cholesky per dual evaluation is cheap. The radial version is block-diagonal: per channel K*N_r <= 128, solvable as an exact SDP in cvxpy/Clarabel within seconds. Constraints: 8 rings x 8 sectors = 64 clusters, giving about 64*(2K + 4*K(K-1)/2) multipliers (~1150 at K = 3). Adversaries in the same class, scored by cloak2d at complex k (layered designs, constant real eps is its own continuation), are the de_ext_B0.1_L8 and p1_optimize_layers_ref designs; also a ceviche or NGSolve free-form adversary at complex frequency (validated against the cloak2d bare M_L first). Environment caveat: rebuild .venv first; its site-packages are currently missing.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) Reproduce first: Hashemi/Strekha identity M_L = Im F(k~) = 5.52 a for the bare PEC by both routes; G_obj reproduces cloak2d b_n at k~ to 1e-6. Replicate Strekha's published qualitative trend (bound ratio growing linearly in dw/w0, then saturating) on their penetrable case, chi_obj = 4 + 1e-3i, chi_clk = 5, R_obj = lambda0/4, R_des = 3 lambda0/4. (ii) K = 1 must equal the single-z Strekha-type dual exactly. (iii) chi_max -> 0 gives the bare value (P forced to 0). (iv) Unit test: every layered baseline design's own fields satisfy all self and cross constraints to 1e-10, while an acausal design with eps < 1 violates the sign implicit in the binary constraint. (v) Monotone non-increasing in eps_max and b/a. (vi) The bound must lie at or below every adversary on the same window.
strategies.expected_tightness: At moderate eta (the card's B = 0.1, eta = 0.05 k_c) Strekha-type gaps are about 2-500x; the ties should cut this most where the single-z relaxation exploits effective loss inconsistently across the window, plausibly by a factor of 2-5. At small eta the single-z bound vanishes like eta for lossless chi; the hope is that ties to an anchor keep it finite. That is untested and is the key experiment.
strategies.closest_prior: Strekha et al. PRA 110, 063513 (2024), with its cross-angle constraints (Eq. 11); here the scenarios are frequencies and the object is PEC. Shim, Kuang, Lin & Miller arXiv 2112.10816 and Molesky et al. PRR 4, 013020 (2022): cross-correlation constraints at real frequencies, not complex-frequency windows, no cloaking. Kuang & Miller PRL 125, 263607 (2020): most-violated-constraint iteration. No prior bound for a PEC object, nor any bound that uses non-dispersiveness of the cloak material across frequencies.
strategies.risk: Medium-high. (1) Ties among homogeneous quadratic constraints can be satisfied by lifted solutions with uncorrelated cross-blocks. While checking the per-channel route for P4 at B = 0, I found that a Shor relaxation with homogeneous cross-channel ties absorbs any cross-channel mismatch into PSD slack that does not touch a linear objective. It collapses to the sum of per-channel minima (~0.007 a), which is why this strategy targets B > 0. Here the effective loss at Im z > 0 makes each scenario's own constraints bite, but the gain from the ties may still be modest. (2) The windows are Lorentzian mixtures, not flat. (3) Overlaps in infrastructure with S2's m(z0) dual (shared G_obj code; different metric and constraint family). (4) The bound is for the discretised operator.

strategies.name: D3: Interval-robust Lagrange certificates, turning sampled-frequency QCQP bounds into rigorous continuous flat-band bounds for quadratic (non-analytic) metrics, applied to the sector metric with cross-frequency ties
strategies.cards: P2 (primary: first certified number for an angle-limited, intensity-only metric on a flat window); P1 (flat-window extinction, same machinery)
strategies.claim: Split the band I = [k_c(1 - B/2), k_c(1 + B/2)] into K sub-intervals I_j of width h_j. By Fubini, for any design, <g>_B = E_{kappa ~ Unif(prod_j I_j)} [ Phi(kappa) ] with Phi(kappa) = sum_j (h_j/(k_c B)) g(kappa_j). This is exact, with no analytic continuation. For P2, g = sigma_Theta(k) = (2/(pi k)) b^dagger K b, with b affine in the annulus polarisation P(k) through the PEC-object radiation map. Form the K-scenario lossless QCQP at frequencies kappa. Its constraints: per cluster Omega_m and per frequency, Im int conj(E) P = 0 and int |P|^2/chi_max = Re int conj(E) P (binary closure); cross-frequency shared-real-chi ties int [P_i conj(E_j) - E_i conj(P_j)] = 0; optionally an anchor field at z_0 = k_c + i Delta tied the same way. Its Lagrangian is P^dagger A(lambda, kappa) P + 2 Re(beta^dagger P) + c. Theorem: if A(lambda, kappa) >= mu I > 0 for all kappa in the box, then <sigma_Theta>_B >= min over the box of q(lambda; kappa), with q = c - beta^dagger A^-1 beta. Moreover q(lambda; kappa) >= q(lambda; kappa_hat) - sum_j L_j h_j/2 with L_j >= sup over the box of |d q/d kappa_j| <= 2||d beta|| ||A^-1 beta|| + ||d A|| ||A^-1 beta||^2 + |d c| (resolvent perturbation; A^-1 bounded by 1/(mu - h ||dA||)). The operator derivatives are closed-form Bessel/Hankel derivatives, enclosed by interval arithmetic (mpmath.iv). So L2 = [q(lambda*; kappa_hat) - sum_j L_j h_j/2] / <sigma_Theta,bare>_B is a rigorous flat-window bound (for the discretised operator). The same holds for sigma_ext in P1 (linear objective) and for sigma_sca.
strategies.approach: 1. Derive the sector functional on the PEC-object radiation map: b_n(P) = b_n^bare + linear map of P (outgoing Hankel projections with the PEC correction), with sigma_Theta from the card's kernel K_mn (fastcyl.sector_width). 2. Write the multi-frequency lossless QCQP. The global real-power constraint already implies the optical theorem sigma_ext = sigma_sca per frequency (card P2 why_open (ii)); include it explicitly for the dual. 3. Solve the dual at the nodes kappa_hat (midpoints) by most-violated-constraint iteration and L-BFGS. 4. Certification step: (a) enclose ||dA/dkappa_j||, ||d beta/dkappa_j|| and |dc/dkappa_j| over each I_j with interval Bessel evaluations, or bound them by a second-level grid plus a Lipschitz estimate of the derivatives; (b) verify A(lambda*, kappa) >= mu I via Weyl's inequality; (c) subtract the slack. 5. Refine K (and hence h) until the slack is below 10% of the bound. Cost grows like K, while the slack falls like 1/K. 6. Isolate contributions by running with and without cross-frequency ties and with and without the complex anchor, to show where any nonzero lossless bound comes from.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Radial-design version first (channels decouple per frequency; block size K*N_r = 8 x 32 = 256 per channel; exact SDP or dual in cvxpy with Clarabel/SCS), then free-form with N ~ 600 per frequency and K <= 6, using a Hessian of 3600 or less and dense Cholesky (well under 1 GB). Interval enclosures via mpmath.iv on the radial kernels at N_r points per sub-interval; sanity-check them against dense 1000-point k sampling of q(lambda*; k). Sweeps: Delta in {pi/8, pi/4, pi/2}, phi0 in {pi, pi/2}, B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3}, K in {4, 8, 16}. Adversaries: lossless_sector_B0.1_L8 (R2 = 0.607, adaptive 1.041 a), de_sector designs, and ceviche free-form with near-to-far projection, all scored by adaptive quadrature (verify_quad.py) because of in-band resonances. Environment caveat: rebuild .venv first.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) Design region switched off (chi_max -> 0): P is forced to 0 and the certificate must return the bare value 1.714 a minus a slack that vanishes as h -> 0. This tests the robust step on known data. (ii) h -> 0 recovers the pointwise K-frequency dual. (iii) Theta = the full circle reproduces sigma_sca = sigma_ext (lossless), so the P2 machinery must agree with the P1 flat-window run. (iv) Reproduce known data first: fastcyl.sector_width matches 20001-point quadrature (1.3e-9) and the full circle equals sigma_sca. Also re-derive the card's vacuous Slepian bridge (lambda_min = 3.2e-12 at N = 8) as a floor the new bound must exceed to be useful. (v) The lifted fields of every baseline design satisfy all constraints (unit test), and the bound lies at or below every adversary's adaptive band value. (vi) The Lipschitz enclosures are validated against dense sampling: the observed maximum |dq/dk| must not exceed the enclosed L_j.
strategies.expected_tightness: Uncertain. The robust step costs only O(h L), which is controllable. The real issue is the relaxation: lossless single-frequency relaxations see little (Strekha's dw = 0 bound is proportional to Im chi), so without ties the P2 bound may be ~0. With cross-frequency ties and a complex anchor a nonzero bound is plausible; if nonzero, the gap ratio is probably 3-30 against R2 = 0.607. It would be the first certified sector-metric number and the first flat (not Lorentzian) window bound that needs no out-of-band caps. Unlike S2 it also needs no arc caps and no exponential 1/omega_I amplification.
strategies.closest_prior: No published bound for sector metrics (Hashemi 2012 lists restricted-angle observers as uncovered). Sampled-frequency cross-correlation bounds (Shim, Kuang, Lin & Miller arXiv 2112.10816) bound only the quadrature; the base research flags that interpolation control is missing. Gertler et al. Sci. Adv. 11, eadl3237 (2025) give differential-form QCQPs for quadratic objectives (single or sampled frequencies). Jelinek et al. 2021 App. A: scattered-power degeneracy, which applies only to lossy classes. Run-1 S2 reaches P2 through Poisson-Jensen analytic continuation, a different route.
strategies.risk: High on tightness, low on rigour. (1) Lossless real-frequency relaxations may return ~0 even with ties, for the same reason homogeneous ties collapse in a Shor relaxation (see D2 risk); the complex anchor is the mitigation, and its effect is the decisive first experiment. (2) Enclosing Bessel derivatives rigorously needs care near the PEC boundary terms J_n(ka)/H_n(ka). (3) For K >= 8 free-form problems the dual Hessian approaches the 1 GB limit; fall back to radial designs or fewer harmonics. (4) Rigorous only for the discretised operator; a basis-convergence study is required.

strategies.name: C1: Rotated complex-Poynting ellipsoid (weak-matter coercivity), a convex floor valid pointwise in k for free-form passive cloaks
strategies.cards: P1 (free-form, B = 0 and flat window: pointwise in k, so the uniform band average needs no complex frequency); P2 (same feasible set with the sector power as a convex quadratic objective, the first certified sector floor, in the covered regime); P4 (radial, via the block-separable per-channel version, maxed with the exact Prufer-interval per-channel floor); also covers lossy passive half-disk/box classes (P2 lossy variant)
strategies.claim: Setting: annulus V = {a<r<b}, TM PEC core, k real. G = G_obj, kernel (i/4) sum_m psi_m(k r<) H_m(k r>) e^{im(phi-phi')}, with psi_m = J_m - (J_m(ka)/H_m(ka)) H_m. H = (G+G^dag)/2 and A = (G-G^dag)/(2i) >= 0 (radiation). Polarization P = chi E, total field E = E_d + k^2 G P, where E_d = sum_m i^m psi_m e^{im phi} is the bare-object field. Taking Re[e^{i theta} <P,(chi^{-1} - k^2 G)P>] = Re[e^{i theta} <P,E_d>] and using Re(e^{i theta}/chi) >= cos(theta)/chi_max pointwise gives, for every theta in [0, pi/2): (*) ||P||^2/chi_max - k^2 <P,(H - tan(theta) A)P> <= Re(e^{i theta} <P,E_d>)/cos(theta). The pointwise condition holds for real chi in (0, chi_max], for the passive half-disk |chi - chi_max/2| <= chi_max/2 with Im chi >= 0, and, with a computable constant c_theta, for a box Re chi in [0, chi_max], Im chi in [0, eta]. Reciprocity (exact): b_m = b_m^bare + (i k^2/4) i^{-m} int_V psi_m(kr) e^{-im phi} P dA. Bound: L(k) = min_P sigma(P) s.t. (*) for a set of thetas plus subregion versions (weights D_j(x) >= 0 whose quadratic forms are PSD). Here sigma is sigma_ext = -(4/k) Re sum b_m (linear), sigma_sca = (4/k) sum |b_m|^2, or sigma_Theta = (2/(pi k)) b^dag K b (convex). The program is convex (SOCP) whenever Q_theta = I/chi_max - k^2 (H - tan(theta) A) is positive definite, i.e. chi_max < 1/lambda_max(k^2 (H - tan(theta) A)). Single-constraint closed form: L = -(4/k)[Re T_bare(0) + Re(g^T x0) + (1/2) sqrt(<conj g, Q^-1 conj g> <e_th, Q^-1 e_th>)], with x0 = Q^-1 e_th / 2, e_th = e^{i theta} E_d / cos(theta), g = (i k^2/4) i^{-m} psi_m. Every design satisfies sigma(k) >= L(k) at every real k, hence <sigma>_B >= <L>_B for the uniform window. Matter-budget variant: if int chi dA <= V, add Cauchy-Schwarz int |P|^2/chi >= ||P||_1^2 / V, which gives a curve L(V) with L -> sigma_bare as V -> 0 (OQ16 'amount of matter' for non-dispersive media). Preliminary (done; scratchpad gen_cons/): coercivity thresholds at k a = pi/2: b/a = 1.5 allows eps_max < 6.06 at theta = 0 and up to 13.2 rotated; b/a = 2 allows 2.93 -> 7.0; b/a = 3 allows 1.93 -> 3.25. At k a = 0.5, b/a = 3: 4.63 -> 14.5. Single-ellipsoid floors R = L/sigma_bare at B = 0 (row format: (k a, b/a, eps_max): floor vs best layered L = 8 DE, gap ratio): (pi/2, 1.5, 2): 0.776 vs 0.893, gap 1.15; (0.5, 3, 2): 0.332 vs 0.558, gap 1.68; (0.5, 1.5, 6): 0.9385 vs 0.9566, gap 1.02; (0.5, 1.5, 20, theta = 0): 0.616 vs 0.731, gap 1.19. Nonzero but loose: (pi/2, 1.5, 4): 0.123 and (pi/2, 2, 2): 0.045. The canonical point (pi/2, 3, 6) is NOT covered.
strategies.approach: 1. Derive (*) from the volume integral equation (chi^{-1} - k^2 G)P = E_d, rotated by e^{i theta}. Passivity enters only through Re(e^{i theta}/chi) >= cos(theta)/chi_max, and A >= 0 is the radiated power, so rotation trades reactive for resistive conservation and pays off in radiating directions. 2. Write the reciprocity formula for b_m in the core-regular basis psi_m. G_obj is diagonal in the angular index m, so every operator is block-diagonal: radial integral operators per m. 3. For each theta, check Q_theta > 0 (per-m eigenvalues) and keep only constraints that are convex. 4. Intersect several thetas and subregion-weighted copies (D_j = indicators of radial and angular sub-blocks); search multipliers (D, theta) that keep the combined form PSD (an LMI). Solve the resulting SOCP for extinction, scattering or sector power. Lossless class: also add the exact resistive identity k^2 <P,AP> = -Im <P,E_d>, relaxed convexly to <=. 5. Radial P4: P_m = chi(r) E_m channel by channel, so (*) holds per channel. The bound is the sum of per-channel minima, taken as the max with the exact per-channel Prufer-interval floor, i.e. the reachable phase interval [theta_n(eps = 1), theta_n(eps = eps_max)] by Sturm comparison. That floor is already computed: R >= 0.267 at the canonical size with eps_max = 2, and 0.814 at b/a = 1.5, eps_max = 2. 6. Flat window: evaluate L(k) on an adaptive k-grid and integrate; L is an explicit analytic-data parametric program, so no complex continuation is needed, which matters for P2, where none exists. 7. Rigour: Galerkin/Nystrom UNDER-estimates <e, Q^-1 e>, so certify with residual a-posteriori upper bounds, <e, Q^-1 e> <= 2 Re <e, x_h> - <x_h, Q x_h> + ||e - Q x_h||^2 / lambda_min(Q). Bound the |m| > M tail with explicit Bessel decay of psi_m for m > k b.
strategies.numerical_procedure: numpy/scipy, plus cvxpy with Clarabel for the multi-constraint SOCP. Per-channel Gauss-Legendre Nystrom (nq = 120-240) on [a, b], |m| <= 25-40. Kernel G_m(r, r') = (i/4)[J_m(k r<) - c_m H_m(k r<)] H_m(k r>), weight 2 pi r. Existing scripts: scratchpad gen_cons/{coercive.py, ellipsoid_bound.py, rotated_bound.py, check_constraint.py, adversary.py}, results {ellipsoid.json, rotated.json, adversary.json}; the rotated run was stopped at the time limit after 12 of 14 points. Sweeps: k a in {0.5, 1, pi/2, 3}, b/a in {1.25, 1.5, 2, 3}, eps_max in {2, 4, 6, 12, 20}, B in {0, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3}, plus sector Delta in {pi/8, pi/4, pi/2}. Adversaries in the same class: layered DE + L-BFGS-B (L = 8, 16) scored by cloak2d with adaptive quadrature. Free-form ceviche designs at (pi/2, 1.5, 2-6) and (0.5, 3, 2-4), seeded by the implied chi = P*/E of the bound's extremal P. Each point takes seconds (closed form) to minutes (SOCP), well under 1 GB.
strategies.known_limit_check: (a) chi_max -> 0 gives L -> sigma_bare (R -> 1), with first-order slope no larger than the Born slope. (b) Constraint (*) holds on exact fields of layered designs (done: 4 random designs, including canonical-size eps_max = 6; e.g. lhs 0.307 <= rhs 0.526). (c) The reciprocity formula reproduces cloak2d b_m (done to 3e-4 to 8e-3, limited by Gauss nodes straddling layer jumps; use layer-aware quadrature to reach 1e-8). (d) Bound <= every adversary (done at 4 points, gaps 1.02-1.68). (e) Non-increasing in eps_max and b/a (nested classes). (f) Radial check: the free-form C1 floor must be <= the exact radial per-channel Prufer floor wherever both apply. Consistent so far: 0.776 vs 0.814 at (pi/2, 1.5, 2). (g) Theta = 0 single-constraint value equals the closed form (0.769 at (pi/2, 1.5, 2)).
strategies.expected_tightness: Tight in the weak-matter corner: gap ratio 1.0-1.7 for thin shells (b/a <= 1.5), small k a, or eps_max <= 2-6, already seen with one constraint. Multi-theta plus subregion SOCP should push coverage to b/a = 2 with eps_max = 4-6. Vacuous at the canonical P1/P4 point (pi/2, 3, 6), where coercivity fails (it needs eps_max <= 3.25 even rotated). There C1 serves only as a regime-complement to S1 and the duality strategies.
strategies.closest_prior: Jelinek, Gustafsson, Capek & Schab 2021 (monochromatic QCQP cloaking bounds, prescribed lossy materials); Strekha et al. 2024 (binary chi, Lorentzian window, bound vanishes as Im chi -> 0 at d omega = 0); Kuang & Miller 2020 (local conservation constraints, maximisation). None gives a lossless, free-form, flat-window or sector floor for the PEC object. The coercivity/small-gain idea is standard in Born-series convergence; the new element is one-sided, rotated coercivity of the Re-Poynting form under the passive class, which turns the minimum-scattering problem into a convex program with a closed form.
strategies.risk: Coverage is limited to the coercive (weak-matter, small-size) regime; it cannot reach the canonical point. Rigorous certification needs a-posteriori upper bounds on Q^-1 quadratic forms and angular tails, because naive Galerkin is not a valid lower bound. Free-form ceviche adversaries may widen the gaps seen against layered designs. The lossless resistive equality can only be added convexly as an inequality.

strategies.name: C2: Shared-matter Loewner inequality: a matrix-valued reactive-power constraint coupling channels (radial) or frequencies (non-dispersive), solved as an SDP
strategies.cards: P4 (primary: B = 0 joint-channel floor; B > 0 with channels x sampled frequencies); P1 restricted to radial designs; non-dispersive band coupling for P1/P4 (same chi(r) at every k)
strategies.claim: Scenarios s = 1..S: angular channels m of a radial design, or frequencies k_j for the same non-dispersive chi, or both. Each has polarization P_s = chi E_s with ONE real chi(x) in [0, chi_max], and E_s = E_{d,s} + k_s^2 G_s P_s. For every weight D(x) >= 0, define M^D_{st} := <P_s, D E_t> = int D chi conj(E_s) E_t dA. Exact consequences of chi >= 0, chi <= chi_max and chi (chi_max - chi) >= 0 with D >= 0: (i) M^D is Hermitian (the cross-constraints); (ii) chi_max M^D - [<P_s, D P_t>] >= 0; (iii) chi_max [<E_s, D E_t>] - M^D >= 0; (iv) M^D >= 0. Lifting x = [p; 1] (radial profiles p_s on Gauss nodes) to X = x x^dag >= 0 makes (i)-(iv) linear matrix inequalities in X. Objective: sigma = sum_s (4/k_s) g_s |b_s|^2, linear in X, with b_s = b_s^bare + (i k^2/4) i^{-m} int psi_m P_s r dr. Bound: L_SDP = min Tr(C X) s.t. LMIs (ii)-(iv) for all subregion weights D_j (radial sub-intervals), (i) as linear equalities, the per-scenario rotated ellipsoids of C1, and X_{n+1,n+1} = 1. It is valid for every measurable eps(r) in [1, eps_max]. The single new element is the Loewner (matrix) form of the gray-chi passivity bound. It encodes that all scenarios share the same pointwise chi, with inequalities appropriate to the continuous class [0, chi_max], unlike the binary-chi equality cross-constraints of Eq. 183 / Strekha Eq. 11.
strategies.approach: 1. Prove (ii)-(iv): for each r, the vector w(r) = chi(r) v(r) with v = (E_1, ..., E_S), so int D chi v v^dag = int D chi^{-1} w w^dag >= chi_max^{-1} int D w w^dag, and int D chi v v^dag <= chi_max int D v v^dag. 2. Radial reduction: G_m is a 1D kernel per channel; lossless radial fields are real up to the incident phase, so restrict to real profiles (a further exact constraint). 3. Build the SDP with channels 0..N_c (b_{-m} = b_m by symmetry) and N_sub radial sub-intervals for D. 4. Raise N_c (3 -> 10; an eps_max shell couples channels up to about k b sqrt(eps_max) ~ 11) and N_sub until the bound saturates. 5. Band version: add frequency scenarios at Gauss nodes k_j. Certify the continuous band either by the frequency-derivative energy identity (Lipschitz control) or by reporting the sampled quadrature value explicitly as such. 6. Extract a rank-1 or low-rank near-feasible X to seed adversaries (bang-bang eps(r)).
strategies.numerical_procedure: cvxpy + Clarabel (SCS fallback). Radial Gauss nodes N_r = 24-48 total, channels N_c + 1 = 4-11, so X is at most about 500 x 500. N_sub = 4-16 LMIs of size (N_c + 1), plus 2(N_c + 1) small ellipsoid constraints. Memory well below 1 GB; minutes per solve. Kernels as in C1 (scratchpad gen_cons/rotated_bound.py). Sweeps: eps_max in {2, 4, 6, 12, 20}, b/a in {1.25, 1.5, 2, 3}, k a in {0.5, 1, pi/2, 3}, B in {0, 0.1}. Adversaries: DE on L = 16 (de_ext_B0.0_L16.json: 3.037 a), the S1 DP-rollout designs, and SDP-seeded bang-bang profiles, all scored by cloak2d.
strategies.known_limit_check: (a) Dropping off-diagonal blocks with D = 1 reproduces C1's per-channel radial ellipsoid bound. (b) Single channel: the SDP must lie at or below the exact per-channel Prufer floor and approach it as N_sub grows (gen_cons/perchan_floor.py: e.g. 0.267 of bare at k a = pi/2, b/a = 3, eps_max = 2; 0 at eps_max = 6, consistent with the baseline per-channel minima of 3e-11 / 5e-19 / 4e-10 a). (c) Channel subset {0, 1, 2} at the canonical point must be <= the S1 rollout value 1.004 a (an achievable design). The full bound must be <= 3.037 a (L = 16) and <= the eps_max = 12 / 20 optima (R = 0.404 / 0.378). (d) eps_max -> 1 gives R -> 1. (e) Non-increasing in eps_max and b/a. (f) Every baseline design's actual lifted point X satisfies all LMIs (feasibility check to 1e-9).
strategies.expected_tightness: Unknown, and possibly weak at the canonical point: S1's exact 2- and 3-channel optima are at most 0.07 and 0.185 of bare against a joint design at 0.559, so only N_c >= 5 can see the floor, and SDP lifts of lossless single-frequency problems are often loose. Most promising in the intermediate regime (b/a = 2, eps_max = 4-6; k a = 3, b/a = 1.5), where per-channel and C1 floors are 0 or small but the true floor is presumably substantial. Target gap ratio < 3 there.
strategies.closest_prior: No bound exists for P4. Shim, Kuang, Lin & Miller (arXiv 2112.10816), Molesky et al. PRR 4, 013020 (2022) and Strekha et al. 2024 Eq. 11 give multi-scenario cross-constraints for binary or prescribed chi, as equalities. S1 attacks the same card by exact variable-phase optimal control (moment-SOS); C2 is a field-variable conservation relaxation with a different failure mode. Per-channel sum rules (Bernland, Gustafsson & Nordebo 2011) are vacuous for |s_n| = 1.
strategies.risk: High. SDP relaxations of bilinear lossless constraints may return nearly 0 at the canonical point, as Strekha's d omega = 0 behaviour suggests. Sizes beyond about 600 strain Clarabel on 8 GB. The band version needs a rigorous interpolation certificate. Discretisation of p must be treated as relaxation-safe: constraints are imposed on quadrature functionals, so the bound remains valid only if quadrature errors are bounded.

strategies.name: C3: Poynting-flux transport delay–bandwidth floor: Beckmann/W1 detour cost around the core, energy velocity <= c, and the lossless energy theorem
strategies.cards: P1 (flat window, ANY eps_max including eps_max -> infinity, free-form); P3 (causal Lorentz media in the lossless limit, including in-band eps < 1, via the Brillouin energy density; low-loss correction for gamma_min > 0); P4 band
strategies.claim: Three exact ingredients give a bandwidth floor for every lossless passive cloak with eps(x) >= 1 (or lossless Lorentz media, where d(omega eps)/d omega >= 1). (1) Energy velocity: time-averaged |S| <= w / sqrt(eps) <= w pointwise (AM-GM on |E||H|), and for Lorentz media w_Brillouin >= |S| since d(omega eps)/d omega >= 1. (2) Flux conservation: div S = 0 in the lossless annulus, S . n = 0 on the PEC (E_z = 0). By Beckmann/Kantorovich duality, int_{a<r<b} |S| dA >= oint_{r=b} u* S_n dl, where u* is the optimal 1-Lipschitz potential in the annulus's geodesic metric. For an exact plane-wave exterior this equals |S0| (pi b^2 + DeltaW), against |S0| pi b^2 for the vacuum disk. Computed by LP (done): DeltaW = 0.2256 a^2 (b = 3a), 0.3468 a^2 (b = 2a), 0.4799 a^2 (b = 1.5a); the mirror plan is optimal. (3) Lossless energy theorem (exact; Green's identity on the k-differentiated Helmholtz equation, with E = 0 on r = a): U(k) = (1/4) int (eps |E|^2 + |grad E|^2/k^2) = U_b(k; {b_n(k)}, {d_k b_n(k)}), an explicit functional of the exterior expansion at r = b, with U_b(k; 0, 0) = |S0| pi b^2. Hence at every real k: U_b(k; b, b') - U_b(k; 0, 0) >= |S0| DeltaW + oint u* (S_n - S_n^inc) dl, a constraint linear plus quadratic in (b, b'). Its leading term is linear in d_k b. Over a band, small b(k) forces d_k b ~ tau_min = DeltaW/(2b) (the minimal excess group delay), so b cannot stay small. Claim: <sigma_ext>_B >= min over trajectories b(k) of the band integral subject to the inequality at every k (a 1D variational program), giving L3 ~ C (k_c B tau_min)^2 (Hashemi-type B^2 scaling), independent of eps_max.
strategies.approach: 1. Prove the pointwise inequality |S| <= w (also for Lorentz media via the Brillouin density) and the Beckmann duality bound with boundary data S_n on r = b, written explicitly in b_n (incident, interference and scattered terms). 2. Compute u* and W1 in the annulus's geodesic metric. For the plane-wave boundary flux the mirror plan is optimal (LP check done), so u* is the geodesic potential of the mirror geometry. 3. Derive U_b exactly: -2k int eps |E|^2 = oint (conj(E) d_r d_k E - d_k E d_r conj(E)) and int |grad E|^2 = k^2 int eps |E|^2 + Re oint conj(E) d_r E. Evaluate both at r = b with E = sum i^n [J_n + b_n H_n] e^{in phi}, including d_k of the Bessel functions. 4. Combine into the per-k inequality, then solve the band variational problem min int sigma_ext dk s.t. the inequality holds on the band (discretise b_n(k) on a k-grid with a derivative stencil and a rigorous Lipschitz remainder; channel tail |n| > N bounded by Bessel decay). 5. For P3 add the loss term: with gamma > 0 the energy theorem acquires an absorption correction bounded via the f-sum budget, or treat gamma_min -> 0 as the class.
strategies.numerical_procedure: W1 by scipy linprog (HiGHS) on 100-400 boundary nodes per side (done: gen_cons/beckmann.py; a -> 0 gives zero excess). Energy theorem: verify U_b against direct field integration of layered designs (radial ODE fields as in gen_cons/check_constraint.py), target 1e-8, for the bare PEC, the P1 optimum (de_ext_B0.1_L8) and Lorentz designs (lorentz_W*.json). Band program: convex QP/SOCP in the b_n(k) samples (cvxpy) with K = 41-81 k-nodes and |n| <= 12. Sweeps: B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3}, b/a in {1.25, 1.5, 2, 3}, all eps_max (the bound does not depend on it). Each step takes seconds.
strategies.known_limit_check: (a) a -> 0 gives DeltaW -> 0 (done: -1e-5), so no floor for the vacuum. (b) The mirror plan equals the LP optimum (done, to 1e-4). (c) The energy theorem reproduces directly integrated stored energy for layered designs, and its frequency-derivative content reproduces the Wigner-Smith delay of the bare PEC. (d) The per-k inequality U >= |S0|(pi b^2 + DeltaW) + corrections holds for every baseline design (P1, P3, P4 files). (e) The premise must fail for the acausal class: some constant eps < 1 design (acausal_*.json) should violate |S| <= w, showing why the class excludes it. (f) B -> 0 gives L3 -> 0, and the bound scales as B^2 for small B (cf. Hashemi et al. 2011, bandwidth inversely proportional to delay). (g) The final band floor must be <= every adversary in P1/P3/P4, including eps_max = 12/20 designs.
strategies.expected_tightness: Loose in absolute terms. The detour delay is small for b = 3a (tau_min = 0.038 a/c; the central ray's excess is 0.34 a), so the expected R is about 1e-6 at the canonical B = 0.1, rising to about 1e-3 for b/a = 1.5 at B = 0.3. Its value is coverage, not tightness. It is the only proposed floor independent of eps_max (valid as eps_max -> infinity, where C1, C2 and S1 floors vanish or are unavailable), valid for free-form designs, and covering causal dispersive media with eps < 1 (P3's W -> infinity limit). It would also make the Hashemi/Chen/Craeye delay arguments rigorous for arbitrary, non-transformation-optics 2D cloaks of a PEC core.
strategies.closest_prior: Hashemi, Zhang, Joannopoulos & Johnson PRL 104, 253903 (2010) (1D ground-plane delay-bandwidth); Hashemi et al. PRA 84, 023815 (2011) (transformation cloaks only); Chen et al. PRB 76, 241104 (2007) and Craeye & Bhattacharya IEEE TAP 60, 3516 (2012) (heuristic; tutorial Eq. 217); Loudon 1970 (energy velocity <= c in Lorentz media); Beckmann / Kantorovich W1 duality (optimal transport). No rigorous free-form delay-bandwidth cloaking bound exists.
strategies.risk: Numbers will be very small at the canonical point because the geometric detour excess is only 0.8% of pi b^2. Strengthening it would need a rigorous lower bound on near-core reactive energy (w - |S|), which is not yet available. The plane-wave energy theorem needs careful exact boundary terms, including evanescent channels and truncation. With gamma_min > 0, P3 needs an absorption correction to the energy theorem. Converting the per-k derivative constraint to a band floor needs a rigorous 1D variational solution, not just a scaling estimate.

strategies.name: M1: Continuum-angle Fejer-Riesz (trig-SOS) local-conservation dual for intensity and sector metrics at real frequency, in the polar harmonic basis of the PEC-object Green's function
strategies.cards: P2 (primary: B = 0 sector floor, plus the Delta and phi0 variants); P1 and P4 at B = 0 (the same program with the total-scattering objective; lossless means sigma_ext = sigma_sca)
strategies.claim: Class: lossless, non-dispersive real chi(r, phi) in [0, chi_max] on a < r < b, PEC core, TM; free-form, including gray levels (the weak-* closure). Exact pointwise characterisation: p = chi E with chi in [0, chi_max] iff, for every point (r, phi), Im(conj(E) p) = 0 and chi_max Re(conj(E) p) - |p|^2 >= 0, where E = E_d + G_obj p. G_obj is diagonal in the angular harmonic n: g_n(r, r') = (i/4)[J_n(k r<) H_n(k r>) - c_n H_n(kr) H_n(kr')], with c_n = J_n(ka)/H_n(ka). Also b_n = b_n^bare + i^{-n}(i pi k^2/2) int psi_n p_n r dr, with psi_n = J_n - c_n H_n. Bound: for any real trig polynomials lambda_i(phi) and any nonnegative trig polynomials mu_i(phi) = |q_i(e^{i phi})|^2 on radial nodes r_i (Fejer-Riesz: every nonnegative trig polynomial is a modulus squared, so this parametrisation is unconstrained and exact), let L(p) = sigma_Theta(p) - sum_i W_i int [lambda_i Im(conj(E) p) + mu_i (chi_max Re(conj(E) p) - |p|^2)] dphi = p^H H p + 2 Re(h^H p) + c. If H > 0 (positive definite), then sigma_Theta(design) >= g(lambda, mu) = c - h^H H^{-1} h for every design in the class. So L2(B = 0) >= max g / sigma_Theta,bare. Multiplication by mu_i(phi) is a Toeplitz operator coupling n to n + q, which the sector objective (Toeplitz kernel K_mn = 2 e^{i(n-m)phi0} sin((n-m)Delta)/(n-m)) needs. Angle-constant multipliers (degree M = 0) are the special case that decouples per n.
strategies.approach: 1. Harmonic Nystrom VIE with the analytic PEC-object Green's function. Done: it reproduces cloak2d b_n of the L = 16 P4/P1 optimum to 1.2e-4, converging with refinement (1.8e-3, 5.0e-4, 1.2e-4 at 64/128/256 nodes). 2. Write the pointwise constraints in the harmonic basis: conj(E) p on ring i is a trig polynomial of degree 2N whose coefficients are bilinear in (E_n, p_n). 3. Lagrangian with angle-dependent multipliers mu_i = |q_i|^2 (degree M <= 2N) and lambda_i (degree <= 2N). Assemble the block-Toeplitz H; the dual value comes from one Cholesky solve, and the Danskin gradient from the constraint residuals at p* = -H^{-1} h (chain rule through q_i). 4. Maximise with L-BFGS on (lambda, q) from a max-margin feasible start (phase 1: maximise lambda_min(H)). 5. Rigour: (a) include harmonics |n| <= N_tail, where chi_max ||Sym G_n|| < 1 plus a margin (about 25-30 at the canonical point; cheap, because H is banded in n); (b) certify H >= 0 on |n| > N_tail by a Schur-test bound on the static-limit kernel, ||2 pi k^2 g_n|| <= k^2 (b^2 - a^2)/(2|n|) * (1 + O(kb/n)^2), with the Toeplitz multiplier norms bounded by ||mu||_inf and ||lambda||_inf; (c) a radial-discretisation convergence study (Gauss panels aligned to rings). 6. Sector variants: Delta in {pi/8, pi/4, pi/2}, phi0 in {pi, pi/2}; total-scattering objective for P1/P4 at B = 0.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Prototype already run (scratchpad gen_metric/: vie.py, phase1.py, joint_dual.py, dual_ascent.py, adv_small.py, *.json), using the Meep env python because the project .venv has lost its site-packages and has no cvxpy. Findings: (i) per-channel phase-1 at chi_max = 5: node-local angle-constant multipliers make n = 0..3 strictly feasible but leave n = 4..6 marginal (lambda_min about -4e-5 to -6e-4). chi_max Sym(G_n) has top eigenvalues 4.0-5.4 > 1 there: near-bound whispering-gallery directions, which are why lossless real-k duals are fragile. (ii) Joint shared multipliers including the objective term are strictly feasible at chi_max = 0.5 / 1 / 5 (N = 6, 16 nodes). (iii) eps_max = 1.5, total scattering, B = 0: certified (discretised, |n| <= 6) dual bound sigma >= 0.696 a, i.e. R >= 0.128 (4 starts agree to 1e-7), against the layered adversary R = 0.724 (L = 8, 24 starts). So the lossless real-frequency dual is nonzero, contrary to the expectation that it scales with Im chi. Runs at chi_max = 1 and 5 and for the sector metric were still in progress at write-up. Next: (a) the full tail N_tail ~ 30 with the analytic tail certificate; (b) angle-dependent multipliers of degree M in {2, 4, 8} for the sector objective; (c) replace L-BFGS with an exact cvxpy SDP (Clarabel/SCS) once the venv is repaired; per-harmonic blocks are about 64 x 64, and the Toeplitz coupling with M = 8 gives a banded H of about 60 harmonics x 64 nodes, so each Cholesky is under 1 s and under 1 GB; (d) sweeps eps_max in {1.5, 2, 4, 6, 12}, b/a in {1.5, 2, 3}, Delta in {pi/8, pi/4, pi/2}; (e) adversaries: cloak2d.optimize_layers, run_de.py sector, and ceviche free-form with near-to-far projection. Report the gap ratio in result.json.
strategies.known_limit_check: (1) The VIE reproduces cloak2d b_n (done, 1.2e-4). (2) eps_max -> 1 must give L -> 1; chi_max = 0.5 already gives 0.128 at R_adv 0.724; check monotone approach as chi_max -> 0. (3) Non-increasing in eps_max and b/a (nested classes). (4) Primal self-consistency: substituting any design's exact fields (rank one) must satisfy every pointwise constraint to round-off, and g <= that design's sigma for every baseline design (P1/P4 de_ext_B0.0_L16 at 3.037 a; P2 de_sector_B0.0_L8 at R2 = 0.391). (5) The acausal class (chi in [-11, 9], replacing the box constraint with |p|^2 <= ... for the signed interval) must give <= 0.00029 x bare at B = 0. (6) The M = 0 (angle-constant) case must reproduce the prototype numbers. (7) The full-circle sector must reproduce the total-scattering bound.
strategies.expected_tightness: Prototype gap at eps_max = 1.5 (B = 0, total scattering, angle-constant node-local multipliers): 0.724 / 0.128 = 5.7. Angle-dependent multipliers and full pointwise-in-r resolution should tighten this. For the sector metric, angle-constant multipliers cannot adapt to the broken rotational symmetry, so the Fejer-Riesz multipliers are the essential element. At eps_max = 6 the near-resonant whispering-gallery channels (n ~ 4-11) will erode the bound. Expect gap ratios of about 3-10 at canonical eps_max = 6 if the bound stays nonzero, and better at low contrast.
strategies.closest_prior: Kuang & Miller, PRL 125, 263607 (2020) (local conservation constraints, finitely many weighting functions); Strekha et al., PRA 110, 063513 (2024) (subregion constraints, penetrable object, complex frequency, fixed chi); Angeris, Vuckovic & Boyd 2019/2021 (diagonal-physics duals); Fejer-Riesz / trig-SOS LMIs from FIR magnitude design (Wu, Boyd & Vandenberghe 1996; Dumitrescu 2007). No prior bound exists for sector metrics, and no lossless real-frequency PEC-object cloaking bound exists.
strategies.risk: High at canonical contrast. Lossless real-frequency relaxations admit near-bound-state (whispering-gallery) directions, so the dual may be feasible only with a tiny margin and the bound may collapse toward 0 as N_tail and resolution grow (the n = 4-6 marginality at chi_max = 5 is the warning sign). The bound is valid only after the Bessel-tail certificate is done rigorously. The Nystrom radial discretisation is an approximation unless replaced by ring-averaged Galerkin constraints. L-BFGS dual ascent gives valid but possibly suboptimal certificates. The project .venv is broken (no site-packages, no cvxpy), so the SDP solve is blocked until it is repaired.

strategies.name: M2: Shift-averaged frequency combs: continuous flat-band bounds for quadratic (intensity and sector) metrics from multi-frequency cross-constrained duals, with no analytic continuation
strategies.cards: P2 (primary: B = 0.1 flat band, where no single-solve reduction exists); P1 flat window (sigma_sca = sigma_ext for lossless, avoiding Lorentzian tails); P3 <sigma_sca>_B (absorbing Lorentz class)
strategies.claim: Exact identity: split the band into K intervals of width h = k_c B / K with left ends k_i. Then int_band sigma dk = int_0^h sum_i sigma(k_i + s) ds. For each shift s, one design is shared by all K frequencies, so sum_i sigma(k_i + s) >= D_K(s; theta), where D_K is the multi-frequency Lagrange dual with multipliers theta. Hence <sigma_Theta>_B >= (1/(k_c B)) int_0^h D_K(s; theta(s)) ds. For fixed multipliers, D_K(s; theta) is design-independent and explicit in s, so the s-integral is certified by derivative-bounded quadrature or interval arithmetic in s. Cross-frequency constraints for real chi in [0, chi_max] hold pointwise: conj(E_j) p_i - conj(p_j) E_i = 0, and the K x K matrix inequality chi_max [conj(E_j) p_i]_{ij} - [conj(p_j) p_i]_{ij} >= 0 (it equals (chi_max chi - chi^2) times the Gram matrix of the E_i). In the dual these give PSD-matrix multipliers per node. With angle-constant multipliers everything still decouples per harmonic n, into K * N_r blocks.
strategies.approach: 1. Reuse M1's harmonic VIE at real k_i + s; G_n, E_d, F and the sector kernel are analytic in k. 2. Build the K-scenario Lagrangian with self constraints (per frequency) and cross constraints (matrix multipliers M(x) >= 0, parametrised as M = Q Q^H), plus the antisymmetric equality multipliers. 3. For each s on a grid, maximise D_K by L-BFGS from the s-neighbour's multipliers (continuation). 4. Certify between grid points: with theta fixed on [s_l, s_{l+1}], check H(s) > 0 via lambda_min(H(s_l)) > sup ||dH/ds|| (s_{l+1} - s_l), using closed-form Bessel derivative bounds, and lower-bound the integral of D_K(s; theta) by the trapezoid rule minus a second-derivative remainder. 5. K = 1 gives the frequency-decoupled bound (the average of pointwise single-frequency bounds). Increase K (2, 4, 8) to let the relaxation see that one design must serve the whole band, which is what makes B > 0 harder than B = 0. 6. P3 variant: replace the box constraint with the real-frequency Lorentz disk (S3's lemma at real omega: |chi|^2 <= s Im chi / (gamma_min omega)) and the budget, for the sigma_sca objective.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Starts from M1's prototype (dual_ascent.py: angle-constant, node-local, per-harmonic blocks, Danskin gradients, L-BFGS). Sizes: K = 8 scenarios x 64 radial nodes = 512 per harmonic block; |n| <= 30 gives 61 Cholesky factorisations of 512 x 512 per dual evaluation, about 0.1 s, under 100 MB. s-grid of 16-32 points per comb; total under 20 min per (B, eps_max) point. Sweep B in {0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3}, K in {1, 2, 4, 8}, eps_max in {1.5, 2, 6}, metric in {sector (Delta = pi/2, pi/4), total}. Adversaries scored by adaptive quadrature (verify_quad.py): lossless_sector_B0.1_L8 (R2 = 0.607), de_ext_B0.1_L8 (R1 = 0.582), run_de.py at matching eps_max, and ceviche free-form. Results go to experiments/<id>/result.json with gap ratios.
strategies.known_limit_check: (1) The identity int_band = int_0^h sum_i must be checked numerically on the baseline designs (adaptive quadrature of sigma_Theta(k) vs comb sums; quadrature error < 1e-8). (2) K = 1 equals the average of M1 single-frequency bounds; B -> 0 recovers the M1 B = 0 bound. (3) The bound must be <= <sigma>_B of every baseline design, including those whose sharp resonances hide between fixed nodes (P2 note: 1.018 on 21 nodes vs 1.048 adaptive); rigour comes from the s-average, not from sampling. (4) Non-increasing in eps_max. (5) The acausal reference class at B = 0.1 (R1 = 0.428, R2 for constant eps < 1) must lie above the corresponding relaxed bound if run in that class. (6) For lossless P1 the result must lie below the Lorentzian identity value Im F(k~) for every design (both bound the same design from different directions).
strategies.expected_tightness: At K = 1 the bound is at most the single-frequency class floor (for sector designs R2(B = 0) = 0.391 vs 0.607 at B = 0.1), so the gap is at least about 1.5x plus M1's relaxation gap. With K >= 4 and cross constraints the bound should rise with B wherever the obstruction is bandwidth. At the canonical point the cards say material, not bandwidth, binds for P1 (0.582 vs 0.559), so expect most of the gain on P2 (0.391 -> 0.607) and at small eps_max. Plausible gap ratio 3-10 for P2 at B = 0.1.
strategies.closest_prior: Multi-scenario cross constraints: Shim, Kuang, Lin & Miller (arXiv 2112.10816); Molesky et al. PRR 4, 013020 (2022); Strekha 2024 Eq. 11; tutorial Eq. 183. These are always for discrete frequency sets, so they bound only the sampled average. Complex-frequency reduction (Hashemi 2012; Shim et al. PRX 9, 011043, 2019): extinction-type metrics only. The import strategies S2 (Poisson-Jensen) and S3 (f-sum disk) use complex frequency. This route stays on the real axis and is the first rigorous continuous-band bound for a quadratic metric without analyticity.
strategies.risk: Inherits M1's main risk: lossless real-frequency duals can collapse because of near-bound-state directions, and cross-frequency constraints may not remove them (a relaxation can decorrelate scenarios, Z_ij -> 0). Certifying H(s) > 0 between s-grid points needs margins that may be tiny near resonant channels. Cost grows linearly in K per harmonic and is fine; the dense matrix multipliers with Q Q^H parametrisation may make L-BFGS slow to converge.

strategies.name: M3: Hardy-space (Szego-Pick) fusion of complex-frequency amplitude floors under spectrally factorised Butterworth windows: flat-window sector bounds with no arc caps
strategies.cards: P2 (primary, B = 0.1 and B in {0.03, 0.3}); P1 flat window (forward amplitude); P3 (Lorentz class, analytic in Im omega > 0)
strategies.claim: Take orthonormal weights w_j in L^2(Theta) and G_j(z) = int_Theta w_j(phi) T(phi; z) e^{2 i z b |sin(phi/2)|} dphi, phase-compensated as in S2 so that G_j is analytic in C+ with polynomial growth. On the real axis sum_j |G_j(k)|^2 <= int_Theta |T|^2 = (pi k/2) sigma_Theta(k), because multiplication by a unimodular phase is unitary. Let W(k) = 1/(1 + ((k - k_c)/D)^{2m}) = |w(k)|^2, with w the outer spectral factor (Butterworth poles in the lower half-plane), so f_j = w G_j is in H^2(C+). Szego-kernel interpolation: int_R |f_j|^2 dk >= v_j^H K^{-1} v_j, with v_{j,i} = f_j(z_i) and K_il = i/(2 pi (z_i - conj z_l)). Therefore int W (pi k/2) sigma_Theta dk >= min over designs of sum_j v_j(design)^H K^{-1} v_j(design) =: Q*. Here v is linear in the design-region polarisations at the complex points z_i, so Q* is a convex-objective QCQP. Solve it with a joint complex-frequency Lagrange dual (M1's local constraints, cross-point same-chi constraints; constant real chi is its own continuation). Flat band: <sigma_Theta>_B >= [Q* - (pi/2) int_{out of band} W k U(k) dk] / ((pi/2) k_c^2 B (1 + B/2)), with U(k) = a real-axis channel cap on sigma_Theta <= sigma_sca. For m = 6 and D = 0.8 x half-band the window keeps 99.25% of its mass in band, so the tail term is tiny and needs no complex-frequency arc caps.
strategies.approach: 1. Analyticity and growth of G_j (as in S2, step 1). 2. Spectral factorisation of the Butterworth window and the H^2 membership of w G_j (m >= 1 suffices for polynomial growth sqrt(k)). 3. Szego/Pick bound: the minimal H^2 norm interpolating values v at points z_i is v^H K^{-1} v. 4. Complex-frequency joint dual: at each z_i = k_i + i y, G_obj(z_i) has a definite anti-Hermitian part (effective loss, Kuang-Miller conjugate-frequency weighting), which removes M1/M2's near-bound-state degeneracy. Constraints are pointwise Im/Re conservation with chi real in [0, chi_max] at each z_i, plus cross-point identities conj(E_l) p_i - conj(p_l) E_i = 0. The objective v^H K^{-1} v is a PSD quadratic in the stacked polarisations. 5. Optimise over points (y, spacing, count), window (m, D) and number of weights J (top Slepian-type singular vectors of the restricted far-field map). 6. Rigorous real-axis tail cap U(k) for sigma_Theta: channel count with a Bessel tail for radius b, plus mirror-frequency handling.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (gen_metric/szego_check.py, szego_check.json): backscatter amplitude G = T(pi; k) e^{2ikb}, Butterworth m = 6, D = 0.8 x half-band (in-band mass 0.9925). The Hardy inequality holds on all three designs. int|f|^2 vs 5-point Szego bound at y = 0.5D: bare 0.1757 vs 0.1671; P2 sector optimum 0.1229 vs 0.1158; P1 optimum 0.1839 vs 0.1741. That is about 95% recovery, against 6-20% for the best single point (e.g. bare 0.0355 at y = 0.25D). So with exact amplitudes the conversion is nearly lossless; the remaining gap is the complex-frequency relaxation. Next: port M1's VIE/dual to complex k (G_obj and E_d with complex Bessel arguments; fastcyl already accepts complex k). Joint dual over J = 5-9 points with cross constraints: per harmonic, 5-9 x 64 complex unknowns, cheap. Sweep y/D in {0.25, 0.5, 1}, m in {4, 6, 8}, Delta in {pi/8, pi/4, pi/2}, B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3}, J_w (number of angular weights) in {1, 2, 4}. Compare against lossless_sector_B0.1_L8 (R2 = 0.607) and ceviche free-form adversaries.
strategies.known_limit_check: (1) The Szego inequality and multi-point fusion are verified on 3 designs (done). (2) |w(k)|^2 = W(k) to 1e-10 (done). (3) Self-consistency: substituting a design's own v must give a value <= its own windowed integral, for every baseline design. (4) B -> 0 (D -> 0, points -> k_c, y -> 0) must recover the real-frequency single-point bound (M1). (5) Full-circle Theta with a forward-amplitude weight must reproduce the optical theorem / Lorentzian Im F identity when W is replaced by the Poisson kernel (m = 1, one point): int P_z sigma_ext = Im F(z), checked with cards_common.lorentzian_imF. (6) Non-increasing in eps_max.
strategies.expected_tightness: The conversion is nearly lossless (about 95% with 5 points, measured). The complex shift y regularises the dual, so the bound should be clearly nonzero where real-axis duals are fragile. The relaxation gap at z_i (Strekha-type: their complex-frequency gaps are about 2-100x) dominates. Expect gap ratios of about 3-30 for P2 at B = 0.1, better at B = 0.3. Compared with S2's log/harmonic-measure route: no 1/omega_I exponent amplifying relaxation looseness, and no complex arc caps; S2 can be tighter when the floors are good.
strategies.closest_prior: S2 (import mode): Poisson-Jensen on a semi-disk with arc caps (log-subharmonic). Hashemi et al. PRA 86, 013804 (2012), Shim et al. PRX 9, 011043 (2019), Strekha 2024: single Lorentzian (one pole) for extinction-type metrics. Shim et al. suggest multi-pole windows only for linear responses. Classical tools: Szego kernel / Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation in H^2 (Garnett, Bounded Analytic Functions), Butterworth spectral factorisation. No prior flat-window bound for angle-limited or intensity metrics.
strategies.risk: Shares S2's hardest piece: a certified floor at complex frequency for a PEC object plus annulus. Here it is a convex-objective joint dual, easier than S2's |G|-minimisation, but still unproven in tightness. Phase compensation by e^{2izb|sin(phi/2)|} over-compensates (support smaller than b), costing a factor e^{-2(b - R_eff) y}; this is mild for small y, but small y weakens the dual's regularisation. The real-axis tail cap U(k) needs a rigorous channel-count tail. The Szego Gram matrix becomes ill-conditioned for densely packed points; use a regularised or SVD inverse that keeps the inequality valid (any PSD minorant of K^{-1} works).

strategies.name: C1: Kamke-comparison branch-and-bound over shared layer values, made rigorous for all eps(r) by a transfer-matrix averaging lemma (joint all-channel certificate)
strategies.cards: P4 (primary: canonical b/a = 3, eps_max = 6, B = 0 and B = 0.1); P1 restricted to radial designs; P2 restricted to radial designs (the sector metric is a function of the channel phases)
strategies.claim: Class: radial, lossless, non-dispersive, chi(r) = eps(r) - 1 in [0, chi_max] on [a, b], PEC core, TM. Calogero variable phase per channel: delta_n' = (pi/2) k^2 r chi(r) [cos(delta_n) J_n(kr) - sin(delta_n) Y_n(kr)]^2, delta_n(a) = atan2(J_n(ka), Y_n(ka)), sigma_ext = (4/k) sum_n g_n sin^2 delta_n(b) (g_0 = 1, g_n = 2). (i) Kamke comparison (scalar ODE, RHS increasing in chi): if chi_lo(r) <= chi(r) <= chi_hi(r) pointwise, then delta_n[chi_lo](b) <= delta_n[chi](b) <= delta_n[chi_hi](b) for every n separately (lifted phases). This is exact per channel, with no wrapping effect. (ii) Branch and bound over boxes of per-layer values on M equal layers gives LB_M = min over leaves of (4/k) sum_{|n|<=N_c} g_n min_{delta in [delta_n^lo, delta_n^hi]} sin^2 delta. This certifies min over ALL M-layer piecewise-constant designs, because bisecting a constant layer value partitions [0, chi_max]. Dropping channels |n| > N_c keeps it valid. (iii) Averaging lemma (new element): for any measurable chi, its layer-average chi_bar satisfies |delta_n[chi](b) - delta_n[chi_bar](b)| <= E_n(M), with E_n(M) = O(h), h = (b-a)/M. The constant comes from first-order Magnus remainders of the linear radial ODE (r u')' + (k^2(1+chi) r - n^2/r) u = 0 (per layer, ||int (chi - chi_bar)(A1(r) - A1(r_mid)) dr|| <= chi_max h^2 ||A1'||/4), propagated through interval-bounded transfer-matrix products and the Lipschitz map (u, u') -> delta. Because |d sin^2| <= |d delta|: L4 >= [LB_M - (4/k) sum_n g_n E_n(M)] / sigma_bare. Band: replace k by sub-intervals [k_j, k_{j+1}] and enclose J_n, Y_n and delta_n(a) over each (interval Bessel), so the comparison flows bound delta_n for every k in the sub-interval. Then <sigma>_B >= sum_j |I_j| (bound on I_j) / (k_c B).
strategies.approach: 1. Exact layered propagation of LIFTED phases (fastvp.py: per-sublayer Bessel transfer, variable phase re-extracted after each sublayer, unwrapped using monotonicity). 2. Node bound from the two extremal flows chi_lo and chi_hi on each layer, one per channel. 3. Best-first B&B, bisecting the layer whose interval most changes the bound (sensitivity = sum_n g_n |d sin^2/d delta| (delta_hi - delta_lo)). 4. Speed: precompute 2x2 transfer matrices per (layer, channel, dyadic chi value), so a node costs M small matrix products per channel (microseconds instead of 48 ms). 5. Rigour: lift via Sturm zero-counting instead of the unwrapping heuristic. Validated numerics (mpmath interval Bessel, outward rounding) on the final leaf set only. Averaging-lemma constants by interval transfer-matrix norms. Increase M until the correction E(M) is below about 10% of LB_M. 6. Band version via k-subinterval enclosures. 7. The same B&B serves the P2 radial sector metric: node bound = min over the phase box of b^H K b, with b_n = i e^{i delta_n} sin delta_n, computed by a small interval/SDP sub-solve.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (scratchpad gen_channels/, copied to invisibility/experiments/strategies/gen_channels/). fastvp.lifted_phases reproduces cloak2d on the L = 16 radial optimum: 3.0370736497949 vs 3.037073649794914 a. It also reproduces Radau integration of the variable-phase ODE. Per-channel extremal windows at canonical: [delta^0, delta^max] = n0 [0.856, 5.198], n1 [2.144, 6.479], n2 [2.864, 7.304], n3 [3.105, 7.956], ..., n8 [3.1416, 6.276]; n >= 9 is frozen (width < 1e-3). B&B prototype (bnb.py; M = 8 equal layers, 10 channels, plain bisection, 48 ms per node): LB = 0, 0.012, 0.094, 0.252 a after 400, 1000 and 2000 nodes (0.046 of bare), still rising linearly. The best 8-layer design is 3.119 a. A covering alternative was tried: branching on s_i = int chi dr with interval envelopes of the integrand (bnb_s.py). It stayed at LB = 0 after 20000 nodes, because the a-priori envelope (pi/2) k^2 r |H_n(kr)|^2 near r = a is huge for n >= 5. That is why the averaging lemma is the route chosen. Next: cached transfer matrices (target 1e6 to 1e7 nodes within 20 min and 1 GB), M in {8, 16, 32}, N_c = 12, the eps_max sweep {2, 4, 6, 12, 20}, B in {0, 0.1}. Adversaries: DE/L-BFGS-B at L = M and the de_ext_* files.

(b) Single-channel runs must return the exact per-channel window floor (C2) and about 0 at canonical (baseline per-channel minima 3e-11, 5e-19, 4e-10 a). (c) eps_max -> 1 gives L4 -> 1. (d) Monotone in eps_max and b/a. The prototype gained about 0.013 a per 100 nodes, so with roughly 1e3x faster nodes, 0.4-0.5 of bare looks reachable. Against the full class, the averaging correction costs O(1/M). strategies.closest_prior: No bound exists for P4. S1 (import mode) attacks the same reduction with occupation-measure / moment-SOS; its grid DP was not a certificate. This strategy replaces SOS with Kamke comparison plus interval B&B: cost is linear in the number of channels and needs no Chebyshev Bessel fits. Methods imported: Kamke/Muller comparison theorem for ODEs; interval branch-and-bound for optimal control (e.g. Lin & Stadtherr's validated global dynamic optimisation); Magnus-expansion averaging error. Calogero 1967 for the variable phase.

strategies.name: C2: Exact per-channel reachable-phase floor (Kamke) plus S-matrix eigenphase monotonicity for free-form designs: certified, often tight, floors for thin, weak or small cloaks
strategies.cards: P4 (sweep corners: b/a in {1.25, 1.5, 2}, eps_max in {2, 4, 6}, k_c a in {0.5, 1, 3}, B in {0, 0.1, 0.3}); P1 free-form under the incidence-averaged / worst-incidence extinction (new card variant P1-omni); P2 radial (phase box)
strategies.claim: Radial theorem: for every chi(r) in [0, chi_max] and every k, the lifted phase delta_n(b; k) lies in W_n(k) = [delta_n^0(k), delta_n^max(k)]. The endpoints come from chi = 0 (bare PEC) and chi = chi_max (full shell), and every point of W_n is attained (continuity of t -> delta_n[t chi_max]). Hence sigma_ext(k) >= F(k) = (4/k) sum_n g_n m_n(k), where m_n = 0 if W_n meets pi Z and otherwise m_n = min(sin^2 delta_n^0, sin^2 delta_n^max). So L4 >= <F>_B / <sigma_bare>_B, and each channel's floor is exact as a single-channel value. Free-form extension (new element): for a lossless, reciprocal design chi(x) in [0, chi_max] (any 2D pattern), the S-matrix S(k) = I + 2T is unitary and symmetric. Along chi_t = t chi the generator -i S^dagger dS/dt = (k^2/2) int chi(x) Phi(x) Phi(x)^dagger dA is PSD (Hellmann-Feynman for eigenphases, Phi = standing-wave channel fields). So the lifted eigenphases eta_j move monotonically: for every level theta, #{j: eta_j(chi) <= theta} lies between the counts for chi = chi_max and for chi = 0 (spectral flow; S - I trace class). The bare and full-shell spectra are the radial delta_n^0 and delta_n^max. Since sigma_ext(theta_inc) = (4/k) sum_j sin^2(eta_j) |<v_j, e_theta>|^2, the incidence average is sigma_bar(k) = (4/k) sum_j sin^2 eta_j >= F_ff(k), the minimum of that sum over multisets obeying the counting sandwich (it equals F(k) whenever the windows are isolated). Therefore every free-form design has an incidence direction with sigma_ext >= F_ff.
strategies.approach: 1. Comparison windows: two exact layered solves per k (fastvp). 2. Sturm zero-counting for rigorous lifts; interval Bessel and outward rounding for the endpoints; k-interval enclosures for the band. 3. Free-form lemma: derive dS/dchi(x) from the Lippmann-Schwinger equation with the PEC Green's function, and show (k^2/2) Phi Phi^dagger form, using reciprocity S = S^T and lossless unitarity. Prove eigenphase monotonicity for a unitary flow with a PSD generator via spectral flow at points away from the accumulation phase 0. 4. Verify numerically on a non-radial example: the PEC core plus an off-centre dielectric rod via Graf addition-theorem multiple scattering. Check eigenphase monotonicity in t and the counting sandwich. Then a ceviche free-form adversary for the incidence-averaged metric. 5. P2 radial: minimise b^H K b over the phase box (small nonconvex problem; interval B&B).
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (gen_channels/: perchan.py, perchan_band.py, adv2.py; JSON in invisibility/experiments/strategies/gen_channels/).
