strategies.closest_prior: No P4 bound exists. The per-channel sum rule (Bernland, Gustafsson & Nordebo 2011) is vacuous for |s_n| = 1. Monticone & Alu 2016 is heuristic. S1's single-channel subsets give the same radial numbers through HJB grids, but S1 neither stated the closed form, swept these regimes, nor treated free-form designs. Imported: Kamke comparison; Hellmann-Feynman / Wigner eigenphase derivative; monotone unitary spectral flow (Birman-Krein spectral shift); Monticone & Alu 2013 for the spirit of 'positive chi cannot cancel'.
strategies.risk: Low for the radial statement. Medium for the free-form lemma: infinite-dimensional spectral-flow technicalities near the accumulation point, and the PSD sign must be checked numerically before use. The free-form result covers only the incidence-averaged (omni / worst-incidence) metric, not P1's single fixed incidence. It is vacuous at canonical parameters.

strategies.name: C3: Channel-subset consistency relaxation: certified outer reachable sets for all 2- and 3-channel subsets, glued by a local-consistency (Sherali-Adams-style) outer minimisation
strategies.cards: P4 canonical (b/a = 3, eps_max = 6, B = 0 and 0.1); P2 radial; P1 radial at B = 0.1
strategies.claim: Let R_S(k) be the set of lifted phase vectors (delta_n(b))_{n in S} jointly reachable by one radial chi in [0, chi_max], for small channel subsets S. Compute certified OUTER approximations R_hat_S that contain R_S, for all |S| <= 3 with n <= N_c (N_c about 8). Then L4 >= min over delta in prod_n W_n of (4/k) sum_n g_n sin^2 delta_n, subject to delta_S in R_hat_S for all such S. Every true design gives a consistent vector, so this is a valid lower bound. It is at least the best single-subset bound, and usually larger, because it combines constraints such as 'cancelling n = 0 costs n = 1, unless n = 3, 4 move'. R_hat_S is computed by forward set propagation on a grid of the |S|-torus. Over a radial step h, each cell maps to the union over chi in [0, chi_max] of the exact flow image, enclosed by Kamke per-channel bounds plus a direction-preserving O(h^2) pad (within a step all channels advance by s * w_n(r, delta_n) for one shared s = int chi). Cells are marked reachable if any part of the padded image touches them, so R_hat_S contains R_S.
strategies.approach: 1. Choose channels n <= 8 (n >= 9 is frozen to < 1e-3 at canonical). 2. For each pair and triple: interval-DP set propagation on a G^|S| grid (G = 256-512 for pairs, 64-128 for triples) with M_r = 200-400 radial steps, using a shared-s segment enclosure with Lipschitz padding. That is sound, and unlike bnb_s.py it keeps the cross-channel direction. 3. Outer problem: discretise each window into cells and solve min-sum with pairwise and triple feasibility tables exactly by branch and bound or bucket elimination (N_c = 9 variables, tree-width small after ordering by n). Round the objective to its cell minimum, keeping the bound sound. 4. Grow the subset level (pairs -> triples -> selected quadruples {0, 1, 2, h}) until the bound saturates. 5. Band: the k-interval version of every R_hat_S.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Evidence already gathered (subsets.py, L = 16 DE + L-BFGS-B, canonical B = 0; subset_adversary.json; adversarial upper values, not bounds). {0,3}, {0,4} and {0,3,4} reach 0.0 a: channel 0 can be cancelled while n = 3, 4 stay quiet, at the price of n = 1 (about 4.97 a). {0,1,3,4}: 3.41 a found. That is above what the global L = 16 optimum gives on that subset (about 2.69 a), so the landscape defeats local search and a certificate is needed. S1 reported uncertified grid-DP values {0,1}: 0.32-0.40 a and {0,1,2}: about 1.43 a. So pairs with high channels alone do not bind; the obstruction lives in triples and quadruples that contain {0, 1}, which this relaxation targets. Planned cost: a pair grid of 512^2 with 400 steps is about 1e8 cell-updates (vectorised numpy, minutes); triples at 128^3 are about 8e8 (tens of minutes, under 1 GB as bitsets); outer CSP with 9 variables and 64-cell windows by bucket elimination in seconds. Adversaries: L = 16 DE (3.037 a) and C1 leaves.
strategies.known_limit_check: (a) Single-channel R_hat must reproduce the exact C2 windows (endpoints match fastvp to grid resolution). (b) The pair {0,1} value must lie at or below S1's DP numbers (0.32-0.40 a) and approach them as G grows. (c) The relaxed bound must lie below every design (3.037 a at L = 16; 0.404 / 0.378 x bare at eps_max = 12 / 20). (d) Acausal windows -> about 0. (e) Inner check: sample 1e5 random bang-bang designs; all their subset phase vectors must fall inside R_hat_S (soundness test).
strategies.expected_tightness: Pairs alone: about the {0,1} value, roughly 0.06-0.07 of bare. Triples and selected quadruples: plausibly 0.25-0.45 of bare at canonical B = 0 (gap 1.25-2.2 to 0.559), if the observed mechanism (cancel 0 and 1 together -> outer shell excites 3, 4) is captured at the 3-4 channel level. Weaker than C1 in the limit, but each piece is cheap and reusable across the eps_max and b/a sweeps.
strategies.closest_prior: No P4 bound exists. S1 computes single-subset values by uncertified grid HJB and plans full moment-SOS. This strategy instead glues many small certified subsets through local consistency (the Sherali-Adams / local-polytope idea from MAP inference) with sound set propagation (validated reachability; Kamke comparison). Published cloaking bounds are channel-independent or single-channel (Monticone & Alu 2016; Bernland, Gustafsson & Nordebo 2011).
strategies.risk: Local consistency may stay loose if the obstruction needs 5 or more channels jointly (S1 argues outer shells couple up to n of about 11). O(h) padding over many steps may swell the outer sets until they contain the cancelling vector. Triples at adequate G may hit the 1 GB / 20 min limits; use bitsets and coarse-to-fine refinement. Radial designs only.

strategies.name: A1: Lifted Nevanlinna-Pick causality LMI: couples each pixel's susceptibility across several complex frequencies inside the design-region QCQP/SDP
strategies.cards: P3 (primary: Lorentzian metric M_L and multi-Lorentzian windows; flat window by a Poisson-kernel minorant); P1 (non-dispersive special case, where the coupling becomes cross-frequency equalities); P2 (multi-frequency sector QCQP inherits the same coupling)
strategies.claim: Imported theorem: Nevanlinna-Pick / Hamburger characterisation of Cauchy transforms of positive measures. For a passive Lorentz medium at pixel x with strength s(x) = sum_j omega_pj^2, h_x(z) = z chi(x,z) is Herglotz and behaves like -s/z at infinity. It is therefore int dnu_x(t)/(t - z) with nu_x >= 0 and nu_x(R) = s(x). For any z_1..z_K in C+ the augmented Pick matrix M_x = [[s, conj(h)^T], [h, P]] is PSD, where P_ij = (h_i - conj h_j)/(z_i - conj z_j). This is the Gram matrix of v(t) = [1, 1/(t - z_1), ..., 1/(t - z_K)] under nu_x. New element: with D = diag(1, E_1..E_K) and p_i = chi_i E_i (field and polarisation at z_i), D M_x D^dagger has entries (0,0) = s; (0,j) = conj(z_j p_j); (i,j) = (z_i p_i conj E_j - E_i conj(z_j p_j))/(z_i - conj z_j). Every entry is LINEAR in the Shor lift X = [1; E; p][1; E; p]^dagger. Summing over the pixels of a subregion Omega_m gives a valid aggregated LMI, Sum_{x in Omega_m} D M_x D^dagger >= 0, with Sum_m s_m <= W omega_c^2 A_ann. Program: L_w = min sum_j c_j Im F(z_j). F is the total extinction functional, linear in X through the design-region optical theorem with the analytic PEC-object Green's function G_obj(z_j). Constraints: per-frequency Maxwell and local power constraints (Strekha / Kuang-Miller), the S3 per-frequency f-sum disk (which carries gamma_min), the aggregated Pick LMIs, and X PSD. Then <M_w> >= L_w for every P3 design. Flat window: choose w = sum c_j^+ P_{z_j} - sum c_l^- P_{zeta_l} <= 1_I/|I| on R+, where P_z are Poisson kernels with the k <-> -k symmetrisation. Then <sigma_ext>_B >= sum c_j^+ L(z_j) - sum c_l^- U(zeta_l), with U from the max-version of the same SDP. The minorant LP is certified by exact rational-function positivity (Sturm sequences).
strategies.approach: 1. Prove the augmented Pick lemma for Lorentz media with an f-sum budget, including the unused share and any number of oscillators (Caratheodory). Prove that the lifted, aggregated LMI is implied by the rank-1 physical point. 2. Write the PEC-object design-region formulation at complex z: G_obj is diagonal in angular harmonics, with radial kernels from J_n, H_n at complex argument. Check that discretised b_n match cloak2d.coeffs to about 1e-3. 3. Build the multi-frequency lift: per frequency, the Strekha resistive/reactive subregion constraints; across frequencies, the aggregated Pick LMIs (the key new coupling). For P1, use the stronger equalities p_i conj E_j = E_i conj p_j (common real chi). 4. Objective: a single M_L point (compare with S3), then multi-point Lorentzian combinations near the band. 5. Flat window: LP over kernel weights (positive kernels at band points with Im z = eta, negative kernels just outside the edges), with caps U from the max-SDP. Sweep eta. 6. Lagrange-dual fallback, which gives valid bounds at any multiplier, if the primal SDP is too large.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (scratchpad gen_analytic/pick_check.py, pick_check.json; meep-env python, because invisibility/.venv has no site-packages, see risk). 1e5 random 1-3 oscillator Lorentz media (omega0 in [0, 5], gamma in [1e-3, 3]), K = 5 complex points around k_c = pi/2 (Im up to 0.0785). Augmented Pick matrix minimum normalised eigenvalue = +1.07e-6, with 0 violations. Acausal constant eps = 0.5 violates the LMI for every budget s in {0.1, 1, 10, 100} (minimum eigenvalue -3.39 to -2.53). Constant chi = 5 (non-dispersive) has P PSD (minimum eigenvalue -1e-14), but the border fails unless s is large (minimum eigenvalue -9.0 at s = 0.1, -0.005 at s = 100), consistent with the card: a constant eps >= 1 is reached only as W -> infinity. Next: (a) a single-pixel material problem to reproduce Gustafsson-Sjoberg (1 s); (b) a radial reduced model: shared chi(r) on N_r = 16-24 cells, channels |n| <= 10, K = 3 points, 4-8 subregions, with cvxpy + Clarabel, SCS above about 1500 lifted dimensions, under 1 GB; (c) free-form polar grid 16 x 64 with harmonic coupling and SCS. Sweep W in {0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 2, 8}, gamma_min in {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1}, B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3}. Adversary: run_lorentz.py designs scored on the same windows, plus the existing lorentz_W*.json files. Report the gap ratio = best design / bound for M_L and for the flat window.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) The Pick LMI holds for all sampled Lorentz media and fails for acausal constant eps < 1 (done, above). (ii) With K = 1 the program must reproduce the S3 single-point f-sum-disk bound, and with chi fixed at z0 the Strekha 2024 setting, number for number at the same z0. (iii) Single-pixel material tracking: min_eps max_j |eps(z_j) - eps_t| under the Pick constraint must approach the passive-approximation floor (1 - eps_t)(B/2)/(1 + B/2) (base's CORRECTED form of Gustafsson-Sjoberg / Ivanenko; re-verify from the primary) as the points approach the band. (iv) Rank-1 self-consistency: every baseline design (W = 0.5 / 2 / 8, R3 = 0.658 / 0.597 / 0.592) maps to a feasible X whose objective equals its own M_L (adaptive quadrature cross-check). (v) The bound is non-increasing in W. (vi) P1 limit: as W -> infinity with the cross-frequency equalities, the bound must stay below the P1 layered optimum R1 = 0.582 (flat) and the design M_L values (bare M_L = 5.52 a).
strategies.expected_tightness: The gain over S3 should appear only where the single-point optimum relies on a sub-unity Re eps at z0 that cannot be realised causally at the neighbouring points. That is the matter-limited regime W ~ 0.5, where the baseline uses eps(k_c) ~ 0.51 and 2.18 layers, and the gamma_min -> 0 limit, where S3's real-frequency floor vanishes but the Pick coupling does not. Guess: 1.2-3x tighter than the single-point bound on M_L at W = 0.5, so a gap ratio of about 1.5-3 if S3 lands near its estimate. Little gain at W >= 2, where the eps ~ 4 coating needs no dispersion. Flat-window values are weaker, because cap terms scale like 1/eta for nearly lossless media.
strategies.closest_prior: Strekha et al., PRA 110, 063513 (2024): one complex frequency, chi fixed, penetrable object. Zhang, Monticone & Miller, Nat. Commun. 2023 (tutorial Eqs. 174-175): oscillator-measure volume-T model with f-sum and X PSD, but unstructured and in free space. Tutorial Eq. 183: multi-scenario cross-constraints, not causal coupling. Gustafsson & Sjoberg 2010: passive approximation of the material only. Import strategy S3: single-point f-sum disk, no cross-frequency coupling.
strategies.risk: Aggregating the Pick LMIs over subregions may discard most of the coupling: a sum of PSD blocks is weaker than per-pixel blocks, and per-pixel blocks blow up the SDP. The lifted SDP may exceed 1 GB beyond about 2000 lifted variables, which forces the Lagrange-dual or first-order (SCS) route with looser certificates. Flat-window caps may dominate. Pick points must avoid the band edges, where the LMI degenerates (diagonal Im h / Im z blows up). Environment: invisibility/.venv has no lib/python3.12/site-packages (numpy and cvxpy are not importable); the checks used .mamba/envs/meep/bin/python, which has numpy 2.5.3 and scipy 1.18.1 but no cvxpy, so the venv must be rebuilt before any SDP run.

strategies.name: A2: PEC-difference f-sum 'waterbed' identity for Lorentz cloaks, with Euclidean (imaginary-axis) operator bounds and a Stieltjes-minorant LP for in-band floors
strategies.cards: P3 (primary; the exact identity holds for every size, W and pattern); the in-band floor targets the small-W and small-object sweeps (W <= 0.1, k_c a = 0.5)
strategies.claim: Theorem (identity confirmed numerically; proof plan below). TM, PEC core r < a, any P3 design (any pattern, any number of Lorentz oscillators, omega0 >= 0, gamma >= 0), c = 1: (2/pi) int_0^inf [sigma_ext,d(k) - sigma_ext,bare(k)] dk = int_ann g(x) sum_j omega_pj^2(x) dA. Here g is the core's two-sided shadow factor; numerically g = 1{|y| > a}, i.e. a ring at radius r gets weight 1 - (2/pi) arcsin(a/r). Rigorously 0 <= g <= 1, so 0 <= RHS <= W omega_c^2 A_ann. Each integral diverges separately (the PEC gives sigma_ext ~ pi^2/(k ln^2 k) at small k and 4a at large k), which is why the Monticone-Alu 2013 sum rule is vacuous for the PEC; the difference is finite. Finite-Y form: (2/pi) int_0^inf (sigma_d - sigma_b) Y^2/(k^2 + Y^2) dk = Y Im D(iY), D = F_d - F_b, for every Y > 0. Corollaries. (a) Cloaking waterbed: |I|(<sigma_b>_I - <sigma_d>_I) <= int_{R+ minus I} (sigma_d - sigma_b) dk - (pi/2) int g omega_p^2 dA. Every in-band reduction is over-paid out of band by the unshadowed electron count. (b) Euclidean bounds: at k = iY the design-region T operator is real symmetric with V - V G+ V <= T <= V. Here G+ = (-Delta + Y^2 with Dirichlet core)^{-1} is PSD, V = Y^2 chi(iY) lies in [0, s(x)] pointwise, and the dressed background fields psi_+/- are >= 0 by the maximum principle. So Y Im D(iY) = Born(Y) + O(W^2 e^{2Yb}), with Born(Y) in [0, const * Y * W A] explicit. (c) In-band floor: minimise <sigma_d>_I over nonnegative measures on [0, inf) subject to the finite-Y identities with these two-sided bounds at Y_1..Y_M and the waterbed. The dual certificate is a signed combination of the kernels Y^2/(k^2 + Y^2) minorising 1_I. Because 1/(1 + k^2/Y^2) is strictly convex in k^2, out-of-band mass cannot mimic in-band mass to better than O((Delta k^2)^2/Y^4). That gives L3(W) >= 1 - c1 W - c2 W^2 for small W, with explicit c1, c2.
strategies.approach: 1. Herglotz representation of F_d and F_b (both have no linear term), giving the exact finite-Y identity; dominated convergence as Y -> infinity, using the k^{-5/3} decay of sigma_d - sigma_b. 2. Large-Y limit: V -> Y^2 chi(iY) -> sum omega_p^2 (bounded), G+ -> 0, so T -> V and Y Im D(iY) -> (const) int sum omega_p^2 psi_+ psi_- dA. Then psi_+ psi_-(x) -> g(x) in [0, 1] by comparison (0 <= psi_+ <= e^{-Yx}) and Varadhan / Agmon large-deviation asymptotics (the straight path either clears the disk or not). 3. Corollary (a) is algebra. 4. Compute Born(Y) and the second-order bound by 1D radial quadratures (closed form in I_n, K_n) for radial classes, and by the operator bounds for free-form designs (budget enters through sup of s). 5. LP: discretise k on [0, K] with a rigorous tail bound, and certify the minorant exactly as a rational function. 6. Optionally add a band-centred complex-frequency floor from S3 or A1 as an extra LP row: the waterbed and finite-Y rows then cap that floor's out-of-band leakage on the low- and high-frequency sides.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (scratchpad gen_analytic/sumrule_fast.py, sumrule_summary.json): vectorised exact TM single-shell coefficients, trapezoid on k in [1e-6, K] with step 0.002, tails extrapolated. (A) 2D free-space f-sum for a Lorentz cylinder (R = 1, omega_p^2 = 1, omega0 = 1, gamma = 0.2): (2/pi) int sigma_ext dk = 3.11036 raw at K = 40, 3.14163 with a k^-2 tail, against pi * 1 = 3.14159. (B) PEC core a = 1 plus Lorentz shell. Shell to b = 1.5 (omega_p^2 = 1, omega0 = 1, gamma = 0.2): 1.2550 raw at K = 40, 1.5405 with the tail (1.5314 from K = 20), against shadow prediction 1.5487 and full-area weight 3.927, which is ruled out. Shell to b = 2 (omega_p^2 = 0.5, omega0 = 2, gamma = 0.3): 2.2056 raw, 2.4568 with the tail (2.4646 from K = 20), against shadow 2.4567. The observed tail exponent is 1.61-1.70, consistent with Fock-penumbra k^{-5/3}. Next: (1) b = 3 and a Drude shell (omega0 = 0, which changes the DC radius from a to b); (2) the baseline designs lorentz_W{0.5,2,8}_L4_g0.01.json against their own int g omega_p^2; (3) the finite-Y identity at Y in {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2} via mpmath at imaginary k (channel sums cancel catastrophically, so use 50-digit arithmetic); (4) LP with scipy linprog / cvxpy on 4000 k-nodes plus a rational-certificate check; sweeps W in {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5}, k_c a in {0.5, pi/2}, B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3}; (5) adversary run_lorentz.py at small W for gap ratios.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) The free-space 2D f-sum rule (2/pi) int sigma_ext dk = int omega_p^2 dA (the card's 2D form of tutorial Eq. 169, flagged unverified) is reproduced to 1e-5 relative (done). (ii) The PEC-difference identity matches the shadow weight to 0.5% (b = 1.5) and 0.004% (b = 2) and rejects the full-area weight (done). (iii) a -> 0 must recover (i), with g -> 1. (iv) W -> 0: the in-band floor -> 1, with first-order slope equal to the Born perturbation of the band-averaged extinction (check against Lorentz adversaries at W = 0.01, 0.05). (v) Monotonicity: the identity's RHS is non-decreasing in the budget, and the LP floor is non-increasing in W. (vi) Non-dispersive eps (P1) is excluded: the high-frequency transparency fails and the integral diverges; the code must report this.
strategies.expected_tightness: The identity is exact, the first rigorous electron-count statement for a PEC object (OQ16 part 2), and its RHS is tight by construction. The in-band floor is useful only where the imaginary-axis data resolve the band. Expected informative for W <= 0.1 and small k_c b (k_c a = 0.5 sweep), with gap ratio about 1.2-2 there. Near-vacuous at the canonical W = 0.5, k_c b = 4.7, because the second-order Euclidean terms carry e^{2 k_c b} ~ 1e4 and must be combined with a band-centred floor (A1/S3) to say anything.
strategies.closest_prior: Monticone & Alu, PRX 2013 (tutorial Eq. 167 plus monotonicity): integrated extinction rises with eps(0) > 1, vacuous for a TM PEC (infinite static polarizability). Gustafsson, Sohl & Kristensson sum rules and tutorial Eq. 169 (f-sum extinction rule, free space). Bernland, Luger & Gustafsson 2011 (Herglotz sum rules). Cassier & Milton 2017 (quasistatic finite-band Herglotz bounds). Import strategy S3 uses the f-sum budget only at one complex frequency, without an all-frequency identity.
strategies.risk: The rigorous large-Y limit (exchanging limits for oscillators with omega0 -> infinity or gamma -> 0) and the exact form of g need a careful proof; only 0 <= g <= 1 is easy. Numerically the tail is extrapolated (exponent 5/3 assumed), so a rigorous tail bound is needed. The in-band floor is likely vacuous at the canonical point without A1/S3 floors. Imaginary-frequency evaluation suffers catastrophic cancellation and needs high precision.

strategies.name: A3: Mixed frequency/angular-momentum Herglotz cone (Regge-type two-variable Nevanlinna monotonicity) for radial eps >= 1 cloaks, a K-monotone interpolation program
strategies.cards: P4 with B > 0 (sweeps B = 0.3, k_c a = 3, eps_max in {2, 3, 4}); P1 restricted to rotationally symmetric designs
strategies.claim: Lemma (proved by the scalar ODE comparison theorem; equivalently, the Wigner-Eisenbud R-function is a two-variable Nevanlinna function). For TM, PEC at r = a, lossless radial eps(r) in [1, eps_max] on [a, b], let Theta(E, lambda) be the continuous Prufer angle atan2(u, r u') at r = b of -(r u')' + (lambda/r - E eps r) u = 0 with u(a) = 0, where E = k^2 and lambda = n^2 extended to real lambda. Theta is non-decreasing along every direction in the cone K = {(dE, dlambda): dE >= 0, dlambda <= a^2 dE}, because the potential's derivative along such a direction, dlambda/r - dE eps r, is <= 0 for r >= a and eps >= 1. The free target Theta_free (regular at r = 0, eps = 1) is NOT K-monotone, because 1/r > r/a^2 for r < a: the excluded core is what breaks it. Channel n at k is cloaked iff Theta(k^2, n^2) = Theta_free(k^2, n^2) mod pi, and sin^2 delta_n is an exact Mobius function of Theta through exterior Wronskians. Comparison in eps also gives the window Theta(.; eps = 1) <= Theta <= Theta(.; eps_max). Bound: L4(B) >= (1/<sigma_b>_B) min over functions t on the data set {(k^2, n^2): k in band, |n| <= N} that are K-monotone on every data pair whose difference lies in K and lie in the windows, of (1/|I|) int sum_n (4/k) g_n sin^2 delta_n(t) dk. Channel-raising pairs (n -> m) exist only if the band spans k'^2 - k^2 >= (m^2 - n^2)/a^2. That gives a rigorous size-bandwidth threshold B (k_c a)^2 >= ~1/2 for the (0, 1) pair: B >= 0.20 at k_c a = pi/2 and >= 0.056 at k_c a = 3.
strategies.approach: 1. Prove K-monotonicity (comparison theorem for the Prufer ODE, with the sign of the potential derivative along the direction); state it equivalently as Herglotz-ness of R(zeta) on every line E = E0 + c zeta, lambda = lambda0 + zeta with c >= 1/a^2. 2. Derive the exact map Theta -> delta_n from matching to cos(delta) J_n - sin(delta) Y_n at r = b. 3. Discretise the band (k-grid, channels |n| <= N ~ k b + 4) and pose a DP / small MILP: branch integers (multiples of pi) per (k, n), with continuity in k (the pure-E direction is in K, so each channel's branch is locked across the band unless the Sturm windows allow a jump), the K-pair inequalities and the windows. Minimise the band-averaged residual. Every feasible design yields a feasible t, so the optimum is a valid floor. 4. Add multi-line consistency (each data point lies on many lines) and, where useful, Pick / Lowner conditions on lines with 3+ data points. 5. Hand the K-pair inequalities to S1's control program as valid cuts.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (scratchpad gen_analytic/fah_line.py, fah_line.json, fah_windows.py, fah_windows.json; solve_ivp, rtol 1e-10). Along the (0 -> 1) line from k0 to k1 = sqrt(k0^2 + 1), designs eps = 1, eps = 6 and the L = 16 optimum (de_ext_B0.0_L16.json) are all monotone. The free target decreases: 5.876 -> 4.475 (k0 = 1.45), 6.085 -> 5.650 (k0 = 1.57), 9.466 -> 9.342 (k0 = 3). Two-point program (proxy residual sum sin^2(t - T)): minimum residual 0.234 / 0.126 / 0.075 at k0 = 1.40 / 1.45 / 1.50 for eps_max = 2, 3 and 4. The windows alone admit zero residual for eps_max >= 3, so the cone constraint creates the floor. Residual is 0 at eps_max = 6, where the window admits an extra pi winding; eps_max = 1.5 is already window-limited (0.55-0.98). Next: the exact delta map, then the full-band DP with branch locking in k for B = 0.3 at k_c a = pi/2 and for B in {0.1, 0.3} at k_c a = 3, eps_max in {2, 3, 4, 6}. Adversaries: optimize_layers / run_de.py ext at the same (B, eps_max, L = 8 and 16). Report gap ratios. All jobs are 1D ODEs: seconds, under 100 MB.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) K-monotonicity holds numerically for eps = 1, eps = 6 and the L = 16 optimum, and fails for the free disk (done). (ii) A single channel (no pairs) must give a floor of about 0, consistent with the baseline per-channel minima 4.9e-8, 4e-4 and 4.9e-6 a at B = 0.1. (iii) The canonical B = 0.1, k_c a = pi/2 has no admissible (0, 1) pair, so the bound must return exactly 0 there (valid, uninformative). (iv) eps_max -> 1 must recover the bare value. (v) The bound must be non-increasing in eps_max and b/a. (vi) The bound must lie below every layered adversary at the same B and eps_max; any design below it is a bug or refutation. (vii) Exact cloaking of both points must be infeasible exactly when the two-point residual is > 0; check by an optimize_layers run targeting channels 0 at k0 and 1 at k1 jointly for eps_max = 3.

art:F3.closest:
No single prior work derives this bound. Its pieces come from five separate lines of work:
(1) Strekha, Amaolo, Mohajan, Chao, Molesky & Rodriguez, PRA 110, 063513 (2024; arXiv:2408.00710). A Lagrange-dual QCQP bound on Lorentzian-averaged cloak extinction at one complex frequency, using local power-conservation constraints. I checked the PDF: chi_clk(w~) is a FIXED number (5 + 1e-3 i) at the complex frequency. There is no dispersion model, no f-sum budget and no coupling across frequencies.
(2) Kuang & Miller, PRL 125, 263607 (2020; arXiv:2008.13325). Conjugate-frequency passivity constraints and bandwidth-averaged extinction bounds, but for a FIXED lossless Lorentz-Drude material (w_c = 0.3015 w_p). This is the card's K = 1 reduction without the mass row.
(3) Electron-density (f-sum) work on oscillator measures, all material-only or structure-agnostic, with no Maxwell constraints per frequency:
- Shim, Monticone & Miller (arXiv:2103.15697): an LP over oscillator distributions with an electron-density budget; the optimum is a single lossless Drude-Lorentz oscillator.
- Zhang, Monticone & Miller, Nat. Commun. 2023 (arXiv:2211.04457): the T matrix as PSD matrix-valued oscillators with an f-sum. Its SM explicitly mentions Herglotz-Nevanlinna-Pick functions but builds no Pick LMI and no cloak.
- Shim, Fan, Johnson & Miller, PRX 9, 011043 (2019): the material FOM |chi(w~)|^2/Im chi(w~) for a given material, not maximised over the f-sum.
(4) Herglotz and sum-rule cloaking bounds:
- Cassier & Milton, JMP 2017 (arXiv:1610.08592) and Cassier, Milton & Welters (arXiv:2601.02169, Jan 2026): quasistatic only, analytic sum-rule bounds and no QCQP. The 2026 paper cites Strekha and Jelinek as the only QCQP cloak bounds and calls them not explicit in physical parameters, i.e. no one had combined the two lines as of Jan 2026.
- Gustafsson-Sjoberg NJP 2010 and Ivanenko et al. SIAM 2019: Herglotz passive approximation of a material over a band, by convex optimisation.
- Bernland-Luger-Gustafsson 2011 and Gustafsson's 'area from sum rule, height from current optimisation' antenna method: these use the sum rule and the field optimisation side by side, not in one program.
(5) Classical mathematics:
- The Nevanlinna-Pick theorem, i.e. that the Pick matrix is PSD; its LMI form is standard in H-infinity control and broadband matching (Youla, Helton).
- The single-point disk is the Weyl/Schur disk, i.e. Cauchy-Schwarz on the Herglotz measure.
- Bergman-Milton nested disks for composites.
- Shim, Kuang, Lin & Miller (arXiv:2112.10816): cross-frequency field-correlation constraints, but with a known, fixed susceptibility at each frequency.
- The Hashemi PRA 2012 / Strekha identity linking complex-frequency extinction to a Lorentzian-weighted average.
art:F3.what_is_new:
The individual tools are known: complex-frequency averaging, local-conservation QCQPs, the f-sum/oscillator representation, Herglotz disks and the Pick-matrix LMI. What is new is combining them.

(a) The material dispersion becomes an unknown, spatially varying causal field. Each point has its own Herglotz measure nu_x and local f-sum mass s(x), under a global electron-count budget, inside a Maxwell-constrained QCQP at several complex frequencies. Prior QCQP cloak bounds (Strekha 2024, Jelinek 2021) and bandwidth bounds (Kuang-Miller 2020, Chao 2023) fix chi(w~). Prior f-sum work (Shim-Monticone-Miller 2021, Zhang-Monticone-Miller 2023) has no Maxwell constraints. I found no electron-budget cloaking bound.

(b) The main new lemma is the Schur product of the augmented Pick Gram matrix [[s, h^dag], [h, Pick]] with [1; E][1; E]^dag. It gives a cross-frequency causality LMI that is linear in the Shor lift of (E_j, P_j) and in s. I found it nowhere: control and Nevanlinna-Pick uses treat the interpolation values as free linear variables, never as bilinear products with unknown fields. Prior cross-frequency constraints (Shim-Kuang-Lin-Miller 2022) assume a known material at each frequency.

(c) The per-frequency f-sum disk with a loss floor, |chi|^2 <= s Im chi / (Im z^2 + gamma_min Re z), is mathematically elementary: it is the K = 1 Weyl/Herglotz disk and close to Shim 2019's material FOM. What is new is lifting it through the budget and Cauchy-Schwarz into the global l1-SOC optical-theorem constraint ||phi||_1^2/Q <= Im<E_d, phi>. That is a modest step.

(d) The Poisson-kernel flat-window LP (signed Lorentzian weights minorising 1_I/|I|, Sturm-certified) is an incremental extension of the Hashemi/Strekha residue identity, not a conceptual novelty.

Caveats:
- Every listed reduction (K = 1 = Kuang-Miller; single-point Herglotz disk; the S3 single-frequency program; the Gustafsson-Sjoberg/Ivanenko floor) is prior art and should be cited as such.
- The novelty claim rests on (a) and (b) and on any measured gain of K > 1 over K = 1. The card itself warns the Schur and Shor relaxation is lossy (3 points accepted s = 0.6 for a true mass of 0.7), so the gain may turn out small.
- Search coverage: arXiv, APS and Optica via web search, plus full text of Strekha 2024, Kuang-Miller 2020, Zhang 2023, Shim 2019/2021 and Cassier-Milton(-Welters). I did not exhaustively search the acoustics or control literature for a field-lifted Pick LMI. art:F1.closest:
Each ingredient has close prior art. No one appears to have combined them into a bound on cloaking.

(1) Per-channel windows (Stage 1). The Calogero variable-phase equation (F. Calogero, Variable Phase Approach to Potential Scattering, Academic Press 1967; Babikov) with the classical comparison/Sturm result: a uniformly "more attractive" potential gives a larger lifted phase. For a pointwise box constraint 0 <= chi <= chi_max, the exact per-channel window [delta_n(chi=0), delta_n(chi=chi_max)] follows almost at once. The phase-function method was also used for EM coated cylinders in the 1970s, e.g. "Scattering by an imperfectly conducting cylinder with a radially inhomogeneous dielectric coating", Int. J. Electronics 31(5), 1971. The EM analogue is the invariant-imbedding T-matrix method. I did not verify the monotonicity theorem in the Calogero primary text; it is the standard comparison result.

(2) Free-form eigenphase lemma. -i S^dag dS/dalpha is the generalized Wigner-Smith operator of Ambichl, Rotter et al., PRL 119, 033903 (2017), arXiv:1703.07250. For a permittivity parameter it equals a volume integral of field intensity, so it is PSD for lossless media. See also Horodynski et al., Nat. Photon. 2020, and Patel and Michielssen's EM Wigner-Smith papers, arXiv:2206.01403. The monotone rotation of S-matrix eigenvalues under sign-definite perturbation, and the counting/spectral-flow picture, are Birman-Krein / Pushnitski mu-invariant results (arXiv:1009.3726, 1008.1215).

(3) Cross-channel joint constraints (Stage 2). M. Horvath, "Inequalities between the fixed-energy phase shifts", IJCSM 3, 2010: infinitely many inequalities linking phase shifts of spherically symmetric, compactly supported potentials with q <= 1. Horvath and Safar, Acta Sci. Math. 85, 693 (2019), sharpens Regge's inequality. Both were written for inverse-scattering uniqueness, not for scattering lower bounds.

(4) Certified branch and bound. Azunre, Jean, Rotschild, Bulovic, Johnson and Baldo, "Guaranteed global optimization of thin-film optical systems", NJP 2019: interval / Taylor-model branch and bound on a few-layer stack.

(5) Occupation-measure / moment-SOS route. Lasserre, Henrion, Prieur and Trelat, SIAM J. Control Optim. 2008.

(6) Cloaking bounds with the same aim, all in bounds_base_research.md:
- Strekha et al., PRA 110, 063513 (2024), arXiv:2408.00710: single-frequency bound scales with Im chi, so it is ~0 for a lossless cloak.
- Jelinek, Gustafsson, Capek and Schab, Opt. Express 29, 26829 (2021): QCQP bound proportional to loss.
- Hashemi et al., PRA 2011/2012: transformation-optics cloaks only, band-averaged.
- Cassier and Milton 2017 and Cassier, Milton and Welters 2026: Herglotz bounds, quasistatic only.
- Monticone and Alu, Optica 2016: per-channel Bode-Fano, heuristic.

Non-bound design studies of lossless dielectric covers on PEC cylinders: Valagiannopoulos and Alitalo, PRB 85, 115402 (2012); Valagiannopoulos, Alitalo and Tretyakov, arXiv:1211.5551.
art:F1.what_is_new:
The new part is the use of these tools, not the mathematics. Each tool is classical. The combination yields the first nonzero, full-wave, single-frequency extinction floors for lossless, non-dispersive cloaks with 0 <= chi <= chi_max around a PEC core. The QCQP and dual bounds (Strekha, Jelinek) go to zero in this regime. Hashemi covers only transformation-optics cloaks, and Cassier-Milton covers only quasistatics.

Specific new items:

(a) Stage 1 floor. The bound F(k) = (4/k) sum_n g_n m_n(k) is built from exact per-channel windows. At the tight corner (k_c a = 0.5, b/a <= 2) the floor matches the full eps_max shell, which certifies the full shell as globally optimal among radial designs. The mathematics is a near-direct corollary of the Calogero/Kamke comparison, so the new part is the certified floors and the shell-optimality certificate. It must not be presented as a new theorem.

(b) Free-form floor. Monotone eigenphase flow (the generalized Wigner-Smith operator / Pushnitski spectral flow) is applied along chi_t = t chi and along the interpolation from chi to the full shell. Sandwiching the eigenphases between the bare and full-shell spectra gives an incidence-averaged floor for non-radial lossless designs. The lemma is known; its use as a cloaking lower bound is not.

(c) Cross-(k, n) cuts for bandwidth. These use joint Prufer monotonicity on the cone dE >= 0, dlambda <= a^2 dE (the A3 Herglotz-cone idea). I found no prior use of this.

(d) Stage 2 joint multi-channel certificate. It combines interval branch and bound over equal-layer chi, a Magnus/averaging lemma extending the result to all measurable chi, and channel-subset reachable sets with Sherali-Adams gluing. An occupation-measure SOS certificate on the Calogero torus dynamics is the alternative route. Horvath's phase-shift inequalities are the nearest prior on joint constraints, but they target inverse uniqueness and give no numeric floor.

Recommended citations: Calogero 1967; Ambichl et al. 2017; Pushnitski/Birman-Krein; Horvath 2010/2019; Azunre et al. 2019; Lasserre et al. 2008. The novelty claim should be framed as "first certified single-frequency lossless floors", not as new monotonicity theorems.

crit:F1.issues:
Verdict: REPAIRABLE. The core mathematics is correct. One Stage 2 step is quantitatively vacuous as written, and several steps are still floating-point or proxy and not yet certificates.

CHECKED AND VALID
(1) Variable-phase equation. Variation of parameters on u'' + u'/r + (k^2 - n^2/r^2)u = -k^2 chi u, using the Wronskian J Y' - J' Y = 2/(pi r), gives delta' = (pi/2) k^2 r chi f^2 with f = cos(delta) J_n(kr) - sin(delta) Y_n(kr). The atan2(J_n(ka), Y_n(ka)) start satisfies f(a) = 0, so u(a) = 0. Re-run: vp2.py gives 3.0370736497 against 3.0370736498 from cloak2d, and the full eps = 6 shell gives 15.98279 from both.
(2) Kamke comparison. delta' = chi F(r, delta) with F >= 0 and locally Lipschitz in delta, so the phase is monotone in chi pointwise. This holds for any measurable chi (Caratheodory), including signed chi, so the acausal gate is consistent. Every point of the window W_n is attained along t*chi_max.
(3) Per-channel floor. min sin^2 over an interval that avoids pi Z lies at an endpoint. Dropping channels only lowers the sum, so truncation is safe. Gates: chi_max -> 0 returns the bare value; the windows nest, so the floor is monotone in b/a and eps_max. The full-shell optimality certificate at the tight corner follows. All 10 gap ratios are >= 1 (1.0065 to 2.75, perchannel_gap_check.json).
(4) Eigenphase lemma. For a lossless reciprocal design with a fixed Dirichlet (PEC) core, S^dag dS = -2 pi i <psi+|dV|psi+> with dV = -k^2 dchi <= 0, so -i S^dag S' >= 0 along ANY pointwise non-decreasing path, not only t*chi. The design spectrum therefore lies between the bare spectrum (path 0 -> chi) and the full-shell spectrum (path chi -> chi_max). The lifts agree because the class is convex. Averaging sigma over incidence gives (4/k)||T||_HS^2 = (4/k) sum_j sin^2(eta_j): checked.
(5) A3 cone. dq = dE eps(r) - dlambda/r^2 >= dE - dlambda/a^2 >= 0 needs eps >= 1, and Theta(a) = 0 is fixed by the Dirichlet core, so the Prufer lift is canonical. The thresholds B (k_c a)^2 >= 1/2, i.e. 0.203 at k_c a = pi/2 and 0.056 at k_c a = 3, follow from dE_max = 2 B k_c^2. Correct.
(6) Interval branch and bound on M-layer designs. Node bounds from the (chi_lo, chi_hi) Kamke envelopes are valid, and the heap minimum (with the parent bound inherited) is a valid lower bound at any stopping time. bnb_M8 gives 0.252 a, which is below the best 8-layer design (3.119 a).
(7) Local-consistency gluing of outer reachable sets is a valid relaxation. The occupation-measure / moment-SOS dual (a subsolution v with the Liouville inequality checked at both control vertices, since the dynamics are affine in chi) gives valid lower bounds. The dynamics and the cost are pi-periodic, so the torus formulation is consistent. The moment sizes 78/364/1365 correspond to 11 variables (r plus 5 cos/sin pairs) at degree 4/6/8.

STEP THAT FAILS QUANTITATIVELY: Stage 2(a), averaging transfer L4 >= [LB_M - (4/k) sum_n g_n E_n(M)]/sigma_bare
- The step is valid but vacuous at every M where branch and bound is feasible.
- I estimated E from below. The averaging error has to cover, at minimum, the realised phase difference between chi and its layer average chi_bar. Taking chi = chi_max on a fraction of each layer, with 10 channels at the canonical point, gives (4/k) sum g_n |delta[chi] - delta[chi_bar]|:
  - 5.03 a at M = 8, which is above the best 8-layer design (3.119 a), so LB_8 - E < 0 necessarily;
  - 2.42 a at M = 16;
  - 1.18 a at M = 32;
  - about 0.42 a at M = 64 and 0.21 a at M = 128.
- E scales like ~40/M a. "E < 10% of LB" therefore needs M of order 100 or more, with branching over boxes in that many dimensions. That is out of reach of the planned 1e6-1e7 nodes, given the prototype gained only 0.25 a after 2000 nodes at M = 8.
- Repair options:
  - put E_n inside the node bound: widen each leaf's phase interval by E_n before taking min sin^2. At M = 8 the realised errors are only about 0.2 rad for n = 0..2;
  - or prove node bounds for boxes constrained by layer averages;
  - or handle measurable chi directly through route (b) set propagation with per-segment padding, or route (c) SOS.
- E_n must also be a rigorous sup with interval transfer matrices. The Lipschitz constant d_delta F contains Y_n, which is large for n near 9 (Y_9(1.57) ~ -1e5), so restrict the channel set or bound the amplification explicitly.

OTHER REQUIRED FIXES
(a) Free-form lemma: wrong pairing for the windows, and wrong metric for P1.
- The windows must use sorted, spectral-flow pairing, not channel pairing. Channel pairing is not implied for non-radial S.
- In infinite dimension the sorted lift is ill-defined: bare eigenphases accumulate at pi^-, and high channels cross pi. State the sandwich as spectral-flow counts through e^{2i theta} with theta not in pi Z.
- Numerically, sorted pairing equals channel pairing (30 channels) at all 10 gap-check points (scratchpad sortpair.py), so the existing numbers survive.
- It bounds the incidence-averaged sigma, equivalently the maximum over incidence. It is NOT a lower bound on card P1's fixed-incidence R1, and must be labelled as a different metric.
(b) A3 cuts: proxy residuals, missing band step, missed cuts.
- The residuals 0.234 / 0.126 / 0.075 are a proxy and are not certified (as the strategy notes).
- A two-point residual does not yet bound the band average. You need an explicit pairing step: integrate sigma(k1) + sigma(phi(k1)) >= rho over a measure-preserving map phi between disjoint sets of k, with the 4/k weights handled.
- Channel-lowering directions (dlambda < 0, dE >= 0), including the same-k ordering Theta_0 >= Theta_1 >= ..., are valid at every B including B = 0 and were omitted. The "must return exactly 0 at canonical B = 0.1" gate is an expectation, not a soundness requirement.
(c) Rigour items.
- The lift in fastvp is heuristic: it assumes each sublayer adds less than pi of phase, with a 1e-7 tolerance. Replace it with Sturm zero counting.
- The band floors use 24-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature of a non-smooth (kinked) integrand, which is not a bound. Use k-interval enclosures. For the fixed-n Prufer angle, monotonicity in k could help.
- The P2 node bound needs a certified global minimum of a non-convex quartic over the phase box.
- The SOS route must absorb the Chebyshev-Bessel remainder as a margin chi_max * eps * ||grad v|| in the Liouville inequality, and round the floating-point SDP rigorously.
- The O(h^2) padding for R_hat_S needs explicit constants.
(d) Class scope.
- Valid for P4 (radial; single frequency and band).
- P1 is covered only for radial designs or the incidence-averaged metric.
- P2 is covered only for radial designs.
- Not applicable to P3: Kamke needs real chi, and a Lorentz chi is complex and dispersive. This matches the stated class.

Closest prior work, in order:
(1) Strekha, Amaolo, Mohajan, Chao, Molesky & Rodriguez, PRA 110, 063513 (2024), arXiv:2408.00710. This is the same architecture: a fixed object folded into G_obj, an annular design region, and local resistive and reactive conservation in a Lagrange dual, plus Eq. 11 cross-constraints for two incidence directions. It differs in three ways. It works at a complex frequency, so the window is Lorentzian. It uses extinction. It fixes chi(w~), which requires loss, and its single-frequency bound goes to zero as Im chi goes to 0.
(2) Trivedi, Angeris, Su, Boyd, Fan & Vuckovic, PR Applied 14, 014025 (2020), arXiv:2003.00374. Lossless real gray chi in [chi-, chi+], with a background structure allowed. It gives nonzero lower bounds on convex functions of the scattered field only for low contrast or small footprint, using an operator-norm field constraint. This is the direct antecedent of Layer 1's weak-matter coercivity floor and of its regime limit (eps_max <= 3.25).
(3) Cross-scenario equality ties: Shim, Kuang, Lin & Miller (arXiv:2112.10816), Molesky et al. (PRR 4, 013020, 2022), Miller & Monticone tutorial Eq. 183, and lifted shared-structure SDPs such as arXiv:2608.08492 and Gertler et al. Sci. Adv. 2025. Angeris, Vuckovic & Boyd (arXiv:2011.08002) give the per-scenario "for all nonnegative diagonal D" box characterisation and multi-scenario stacking. None of these writes the gray-chi matrix Loewner inequalities.
(4) Rotated combinations of real and reactive power with an angle multiplier are standard: Gustafsson, Schab, Jelinek & Capek, NJP 22, 073013 (2020); Kuang, Zhang & Miller, Optica (2021), arXiv:2002.00521; Kuang & Miller's conjugate-frequency PSD trick.
(5) Jelinek, Gustafsson, Capek & Schab, Opt. Express 2021, arXiv:2103.17210. Monochromatic cloak QCQP, proportional to loss.
(6) The only SOS use in optics found is Chao, Hammond & Johnson, arXiv:2502.09821 (SERS, quartic objective), not multiplier parametrisation.
(7) Off-field analogues: robust control certifies frequency-dependent matrix inequalities over a band either by frequency gridding with Lipschitz or interval inter-grid certification, or exactly by the generalized KYP lemma (Iwasaki & Hara 2005). Weyl and resolvent perturbation are standard tools in validated numerics. - The Fubini identity and Weyl/Lipschitz inter-grid certification are textbook tools; robust control uses the same gridding pattern, or the KYP lemma.

Genuinely new, as far as these searches found:
(a) The first rigorous flat-band (non-Lorentzian) lower bound on cloaking at real frequencies, with no analytic continuation. It uses shift-averaged frequency combs, interval-robust dual certificates between shift samples, Bessel-derivative interval enclosures and a Schur-test tail certificate for |n| > N. Nobody has bounded flat-band cloaking or certified a continuous band from sampled-frequency duals; the tutorial and Strekha both leave this open.
(b) A nonzero lossless (real, non-dispersive, gray chi in [0, chi_max]) single-frequency floor for a PEC cylinder plus annulus. It comes from a rotated-coercivity convex relaxation, Re(e^{i theta}/chi) >= cos(theta)/chi_max, with a closed-form or SOCP bound and an int|P|^2/chi >= ||P||_1^2/V matter-volume corollary. It is new as a local-conservation construction applied to cloaking, but it sits close to Trivedi 2020 in spirit and regime.
(c) Matrix Loewner cross-scenario constraints for gray (not binary) chi, shared across frequencies or channels: chi_max M^D - [<P_s,DP_t>] >= 0 and chi_max [<E_s,DE_t>] - M^D >= 0, with M^D Hermitian PSD. These are strictly stronger than the Eq. 183 equality ties. They are implicit in a full Shor lift of [chi; e_1..e_S], but this explicit form and its use as PSD matrix multipliers do not appear in the literature found.
(d) Angle-continuous Fejer-Riesz (trig-SOS) multipliers in an angular-harmonic VIE with sector Toeplitz coupling. This is a new parametrisation of the known "all local D" constraint family, with a modest conceptual step.
(e) Sector, angle-limited and total-scattering targets for a lossless real-frequency PEC cloak (P2, P1, P4). No prior bound exists for these metrics.

Overall: the dual machinery is prior art. What is new is the certified real-frequency flat-band layer, the gray-chi Loewner ties, and their application to lossless PEC cloaking with scattering and sector metrics.

crit:F2.issues:
VERDICT: REPAIRABLE. The core inequalities are valid lower-bound machinery for the stated class: lossless, frequency-independent real chi in [0, chi_max], free-form, PEC core folded into G_obj. However, the strategy text claims several things its own code and saved numbers do not support, and two rigour steps are wrong as stated. I checked the cards, the strategy and the scratchpad prototypes (gen_metric/, gen_cons/), and recomputed the key quantities. My files are in scratchpad/critic_F2/: checks.py, checks.json, conv.py, conv.json.

STEPS THAT CHECK OUT
(a) G_obj per harmonic. g_n = (i/4)[J_n(kr<) - c_n H_n(kr<)] H_n(kr>) is correct. It vanishes at r = a, and bare b_n = -c_n. The reciprocity formula b_n = b_n^bare + (i k^2/4) i^-n int psi_n e^{-in phi'} p dA is correct; the strategy text omits the e^{-in phi'} factor. check_constraint.py verifies it on exact ODE designs.
(b) Pointwise characterisation. Im(conj(E) p) = 0 together with chi_max Re(conj(E) p) >= |p|^2 is equivalent to p = chi E with real chi in [0, chi_max]; E = 0 forces p = 0. Exact.
(c) Layer 1 (rotated coercivity). I re-derived it: Re(e^{i theta}<P,E_d>) = cos(theta) int |p|^2/chi - k^2 cos(theta) <P,HP> + k^2 sin(theta) <P,AP>, which gives the stated ellipsoid for 0 <= theta < pi/2. The closed-form maximum of the linear objective over the ellipsoid in rotated_bound.py is correct.
- Discretisation converges: 0.77569 / 0.77571 / 0.77571 at nq = 30 / 120 / 240, increasing with nq. The reported floors 0.776, 0.332, 0.9385 and 0.616 match the json files.
- For lossy chi the rotated disk contains the passive upper half-disk only for theta >= 0. A box class with Im chi <= gamma needs tan(theta) >= gamma/chi_max.
(d) Layer 2 Lagrangian. For any lambda and any mu >= 0, L <= sigma on the feasible set, and g = c - h^H H^{-1} h holds when H > 0. I checked the H and h assembly in dual_ascent.py term by term and it is correct. Restricting the multipliers to trig polynomials or Fejer-Riesz forms only weakens the bound, so it stays valid. Angle-dependent multipliers are a tightness choice, not a requirement: angle-constant ones are also valid for the sector kernel.
(e) Layer 3 Loewner ties. M_st = int D chi conj(E_s) E_t is Hermitian and >= 0. chi_max M - [<P_s,DP_t>] = int D chi (chi_max - chi) conj(E_s) E_t >= 0, and chi_max [<E_s,DE_t>] - M >= 0. All three hold for a shared real chi, across frequencies (non-dispersive) and across radial channels. With s = t they reduce to the local constraints.
(f) Layer 4. The Fubini shift-comb identity is exact, and K = 1 reproduces the average of single-frequency bounds. The Weyl step lambda_min(H(s)) >= lambda_min(H(s_l)) - sup||dH/ds|| |s - s_l| is valid. A dual with fixed multipliers is valid at every s where H(s) >= 0.
(g) Limits. chi_max -> 0 gives R -> 1, and the full-circle sector reproduces sigma_sca. Every layer is a lower bound on the stated metric; P1 and P2 are band ratios with an exact bare denominator.

FAILING OR UNSUPPORTED STEPS
1. The prototype numbers are labelled "certified" but are not, because of harmonic truncation.
- dual_ascent.py and joint_dual.py keep only |n| <= 6. For |n| > 6 they drop both the PSD check of H_n and the term -h_n^H H_n^{-1} h_n, which is nonzero because E_d has every harmonic. Since h^H H^{-1} h >= h_L^H H_LL^{-1} h_L, truncation over-estimates the dual.
- At chi_max = 5 the dropped blocks are not coercive. chi_max * lambda_max(Herm k^2 G_n) = 1.57 at n = 7 and 1.15 at n = 8, against a radiative part of only 3.9e-3 and 3.5e-4. So the positive margin of 3.6e-4 in joint_dual_5.0 (N = 6) does not establish H >= 0. The whispering-gallery cutoff is near n ~ kb sqrt(eps_max) ~ 11.
- At chi_max = 0.5 the tail is coercive, so 0.128 carries only a small truncation error. It is still uncertified, because the radial discretisation is a Nystrom approximation.
2. The tail Schur bound is inconsistent with the stated N_tail.
- The stated bound ||2 pi k^2 g_n|| <= k^2 (b^2 - a^2)/(2|n|) is valid but loose. A plain Schur test gives (b^2 - a^2)/(4|n|); the true decay is about b^2/n^2 (measured lambda_max is 0.026 at n = 25, against 0.395 from the stated formula).
- With the stated formula at chi_max = 5, coercivity needs |n| > 49, not 25-30. The 25-30 figure matches only the /4 version, and even that is marginal (0.99 at n = 25).
- The "(1 + O(kb/n)^2)" factor needs an explicit constant.
- Tail coercivity also needs min mu(phi) > 0 uniformly. A Fejer-Riesz mu = |q|^2 can vanish, and angle-dependent multipliers couple the tail to the low block through the Toeplitz band, so the tail cannot be certified block by block. It needs a Schur-complement argument.
3. The claim that the Loewner form is "stronger than the binary equality ties" (tutorial Eq. 183 / Strekha Eq. 11) is reversed.
- Binary chi in {0, chi_max} gives chi_max <P_s,DE_t> = <P_s,DP_t>, an equality that implies the gray Loewner inequality.
- Binary ties are also valid for the gray class. The card's own weak-* density and continuity argument gives inf over binary = min over gray, so any bound valid for all binary designs bounds the gray minimum.
- Repair: use the binary equalities with this justification stated. They give a tighter bound.
4. The OQ16 matter-volume curve, int |P|^2/chi >= ||P||_1^2 / V, holds only with V = int chi dA (Cauchy-Schwarz) and only for real chi.
- Alone it is not coercive: concentrated P makes ||P||_1^2/V - k^2 <P,HP> negative. It needs the chi_max term as well, so it inherits the same coercivity limit.
- It is not the P3 oscillator-strength (f-sum) budget and must not be presented as a P3 bound.
5. The strategy text leaves out results in its own saved files that are adverse.
- dual_ascent at chi_max = 1: ratio -1.4e-5. joint_dual at chi_max = 5: -1.4e-4. Rotated Layer 1 at canonical size: -0.004 at eps_max = 2 and -0.075 at eps_max = 3.
- So at canonical size the single-frequency lossless dual falls to the trivial floor sigma_ext = sigma_sca >= 0 once eps_max >= 2. That is consistent with Strekha's observation that the dual bound scales with Im chi.
- "Coercivity up to eps_max 3.25" therefore does not mean a non-trivial floor.
- The "nonzero" prototype (0.128 at eps_max = 1.5) is barely above Layer 1 alone, which I computed as 0.102 at the same point (and 0.344 at eps_max = 1.25). It is not evidence that Layer 2 escapes the collapse.
6. At B = 0 with one incident wave there is only one scenario, so Layer 3 adds nothing to P1 or P2. The targets "certified P2 sector floor at B = 0" and canonical-size P1 at B = 0 reduce to Layer 2, which collapses on current evidence. The true free-form minimum at B = 0 may itself be near 0: only the radial case has a positivity conjecture (C4).
7. The B > 0 positivity mechanism is analyticity on an interval. Finite-K sampling, with ties at K frequencies, does not encode it. If K-frequency near-cloaks exist in the class, D_K(s) can collapse for every s, so the Fubini integral is valid but may be trivial at the reachable K (K x N_r <= 512). This is a triviality risk, not an invalidity, and the complex-anchor test should come first.
8. Rigour details to fix.
- Layer 4's Lipschitz slack must use the supremum over [s_l, s_{l+1}] via ||A(s)^{-1}|| <= 1/(lambda_min(A(s_l)) - sup||dA|| Delta s), not values at the nodes.
- The continuum bound needs an a-posteriori upper bound on h^H H^{-1} h, because Galerkin under-estimates it. A workable form, for any trial y with operator H >= gamma I: h^H H^{-1} h <= 2 Re(h^H y) - y^H H y + ||h - H y||^2 / gamma. This needs an enclosed continuum lambda_min and residual.
- The gate "rank-one fields satisfy constraints to 1e-9" is tautological in the same Nystrom discretisation. Use ODE-exact fields (check_constraint.py) to measure the discretisation error of the certificate.
- The acausal gate (eps in [-10, 10]) needs the two-sided characterisation (chi - chi_min)(chi_max - chi) >= 0, which brings in a |E|^2 term. The [0, chi_max] constraints do not apply to that class.
- The family's "certified" labels should read "discretised, uncertified" until items 1, 2 and 8 are done.
- Prerequisite confirmed: the repo .venv cannot import numpy or cvxpy. I used the Meep env Python for these checks.
crit:F2.reduces_to_known: Single-scenario Layer 2 is the local-conservation Lagrange dual / Shor relaxation for real chi (Kuang & Miller; Molesky et al.), specialised to a PEC-folded G_obj. It should reproduce Strekha 2024's observation that the bound vanishes as Im chi -> 0, and the saved numbers do: a trivial floor for eps_max >= 2 at canonical size. Layer 1 is the global (Re/Im) power-conservation constraint taken in a complex-rotated combination, i.e. the single-constraint S-procedure / ellipsoid bound. It gives non-trivial floors only in the weak-matter regime (for example 0.776 at k a = pi/2, b/a = 1.5, eps_max = 2; 0.102 at canonical size with eps_max = 1.5). Layer 3 generalises the multi-frequency cross-constraints of tutorial Eq. 183 / Strekha Eq. 11 from binary to gray chi in Loewner form; the binary form is the stronger one. In the stated limits: chi_max -> 0 gives 1, K = 1 gives the average of single-frequency bounds, and the full-circle sector gives sigma_sca. All of these hold.

art:F6.closest: The delay-bandwidth scaling itself is already in the literature, as a heuristic or for restricted classes. Craeye & Bhattacharya, IEEE TAP 60, 3516 (2012), tutorial Eq. 217, is a wave-packet rule of thumb: extra path dR gives delay dR/c and B < lambda/(dR*Qc). Chen et al., PRB 76, 241104 (2007), get B <= dr0/a from subluminal group velocity in transformation-optics (TO) cloaks. Hashemi, Zhang, Joannopoulos & Johnson, PRL 104, 253903 (2010; arXiv:1003.5934) give 1D delay-bandwidth and delay-loss limits for ground-plane cloaks. Hashemi et al., PRA 84, 023815 (2011) prove thickness scaling for TO cloaks with bounded index. Hashemi et al., PRA 86, 013804 (2012; arXiv:1203.2190) give diameter-bandwidth scaling for TO cloaks with bounded contrast. Miller & Monticone's tutorial (arXiv:2605.24738, Sec. 5.7, OQ16) calls all of these heuristic or class-restricted and leaves a rigorous version open. Two of the ingredients are textbook or published. (1) Energy velocity <= c, i.e. |S| <= c*u: proved pointwise for nondispersive media by AM-GM, and for general passive linear media by Welters, Avniel & Johnson, PRA 2014 (arXiv:1405.0238). (3) The k-derivative energy identity (stored energy = boundary term in b_n and d_k b_n) is the Wigner-Smith / Foster / Rhodes-type energy theorem; renormalized-energy forms are in Patel & Michielssen (arXiv:2003.06985, 2005.03211) and an acoustic version in arXiv:2205.07347. The antenna analogues, energy-derivative Q bounds (Yaghjian-Best, Chu, Gustafsson), use the same structure. Abdelrahman, Hayran, Chen & Monticone, Nat. Commun. 12 (2021; arXiv:2011.02333) make causality and delay arguments against fast-light cloaks but derive no bound of this kind. Strekha et al., PRA 110, 063513 (2024; arXiv:2408.00710) give rigorous band bounds, but they are computational and depend on chi/loss and its bounds rather than being independent of eps_max. Chen & Chan, JAP 104, 033113 (2008; arXiv:0712.3985) cover energy velocity for ideal TO cloaks only.
art:F6.what_is_new: No source was found for ingredient (2) or for the way the pieces are put together. Ingredient (2) uses Beckmann / Kantorovich (optimal-transport) duality with a 1-Lipschitz potential in the annulus geodesic metric. This gives a rigorous lower bound on the integrated |S| that must detour around an impenetrable PEC core: |S0|(pi b^2 + DeltaW). Searches covering optimal transport plus Poynting, Lipschitz duality and cloaking delay found no electromagnetic, acoustic or antenna use of it. Combining it with the exact energy theorem gives a per-k inequality, and from that a convex band-floor program (QP/SOCP) in b_n(k) with a rigorous remainder. The result is a floor that holds for free-form lossless eps >= 1 (and Lorentz media), is independent of eps_max even as eps_max -> infinity, and is not restricted to TO cloaks. It turns the Craeye-Bhattacharya / Chen / Hashemi delay heuristic into a rigorous bound for non-TO cloaks of a PEC core, which partly answers OQ16. Caveats: ingredients (1) and (3) are known and the B^2 (Hashemi-type) scaling is expected. The floor is numerically tiny (R ~ 1e-6 at B = 0.1) because DeltaW is only about 0.8% of pi b^2. The novelty is in coverage and rigour, not in a new scaling law. Not checked: Craeye-Bhattacharya and Chen 2007 were not re-verified from the primary sources (only via the tutorial), and PMC8144568 was blocked by a CAPTCHA.
